Plasma-facing limiter. As a measurement locus, 'at_limiter' denotes the scrape-off-layer plasma immediately adjacent to the limiter surface; the DD provides only the limiter surface geometry (wall/description_2d/limiter) and the precise plasma evaluation point is not yet standardised (IMAS_3226). For the separatrix-limiter tangency CONTACT point use active_limiter_point; for a quantity distributed OVER the limiter surface (e.g. a peak power density) use the 'along' relation (along_limiter).

Location of the maximum pedestal gradient (the steep mid-pedestal), i.e. the peak-gradient / fit position of the edge barrier. Distinct from the pedestal top. DD: summary/pedestal_fits/*/d_dpsi_norm_max_position, summary/local/pedestal/position/psi.

NAMES.name: capacitance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Effective capacitance of an impedance-matching element in an ion-cyclotron
heating antenna, relating stored charge to the RF voltage used for circuit
tuning.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the non-negative lumped capacitance associated with an
impedance-matching element in an ion-cyclotron heating antenna module. It
represents the element's ability to store electric charge and participate in
tuning the radio-frequency transmission circuit.

For an ideal lumped capacitive element, the capacitance is defined by

$$
C = \frac{Q}{V}
$$

where $C$ is the capacitance, $Q$ is the charge stored on the element, and
$V$ is the electric potential difference across the element.

The quantity applies to the specified matching element of the antenna and
does not represent the capacitance of an unrelated circuit component or the
entire transmission system. It is a circuit parameter rather than a power,
current, or operating-frequency quantity.

Together with the [resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), it characterizes
the antenna's effective RF impedance; the [frequency of an ion-cyclotron
heating antenna](name:frequency_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) identifies
the RF operating frequency at which the matching condition is evaluated.

NAMES.name: forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Forward RF power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the incident power
traveling from the generator toward the antenna before reflection and
coupling to the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the forward-traveling
RF power at a defined reference plane on the feed line, directed from the
generator toward the antenna. It is the incident power arriving at the
antenna before reflection at the antenna–plasma interface and before power
is coupled into the plasma.

The quantity applies to one antenna or antenna module at its feed-line
reference plane and includes only the forward-traveling component; it is not
summed over an antenna system. It excludes backward-traveling [reflected
power](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and power
already coupled into the plasma.

At a common reference plane, forward and reflected power determine the net
[launched power]: the launched component is the forward power less the
reflected power when intervening feed-line losses are excluded.

NAMES.name: frequency_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Radio-frequency drive frequency of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna,
averaged over its modules. This non-negative scalar sets the ion-cyclotron
resonance layer locations and the ion species and harmonics accessible for
wave absorption.
NAMES.long:
Radio-frequency drive frequency of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the
non-negative cycle frequency of the electromagnetic drive applied to the
antenna. It is an antenna-level setting that enters the ion-cyclotron
resonance condition for wave absorption by ions in the plasma.

For an ion species resonating at harmonic $n$, the defining resonance
relation is:

$$
2\pi f = n\Omega_{ci} = n\frac{Z_i e B}{m_i}
$$

where $f$ is this radio-frequency drive frequency, $n$ is the positive
integer ion-cyclotron harmonic number, $i$ labels the resonant ion species,
$\Omega_{ci}$ is the ion cyclotron angular frequency of species $i$, $Z_i$
is the charge number of species $i$, $e$ is the elementary charge, $B$ is
the magnetic-field magnitude at the resonant location, and $m_i$ is the mass
of species $i$.

This quantity applies to a complete ion-cyclotron heating antenna, not to a
single antenna module; if module frequencies differ, its aggregation
convention is the arithmetic mean over the modules. It is the ordinary cycle
frequency $f$, not the angular frequency $2\pi f$, and it is distinct from
the spatially varying local ion cyclotron frequency in the plasma.

The frequency, together with the selected ion species, harmonic number, and
magnetic-field magnitude, determines which resonance layers are accessible,
but it does not by itself identify a unique absorption channel when several
species or harmonics satisfy the resonance relation. It is separate from
total_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna, from the RF-circuit quantity
[resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna),
and from voltage_amplitude_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna; the analogous
electron-cyclotron quantity is
[frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_heating_antenna](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_beam).

NAMES.name: launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the net RF power entering the
vacuum vessel after reflection at the antenna input reference plane.
NAMES.long:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative net RF power
propagating from the antenna input reference plane into the vacuum vessel
toward the plasma. It is one per-antenna component of the wave-power budget
represented by [power of a lower-hybrid antenna].

The net launched power is defined by:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the incident RF power arriving at the antenna
input reference plane and $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the RF power returning
toward the transmission line. The quantity applies to one lower-hybrid
antenna and is not an aggregate over multiple antennas.

Launched power is distinct from [forward power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna), which includes power
subsequently reflected, and from [reflected power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). It denotes power
entering the vacuum vessel, not generator output or power subsequently
absorbed by the plasma. Mode-resolved representations, including [per
toroidal mode launched power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:per_toroidal_mode_launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna),
resolve this same per-antenna quantity by wave-number interval.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_and_poloidal_mode_number_launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna resolved jointly per unit toroidal
and poloidal refractive-index interval is the net RF power distribution
entering the vacuum vessel from one antenna row.
NAMES.long:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative RF power
entering the vacuum vessel from one selected antenna row, resolved jointly
over toroidal and poloidal refractive-index coordinates. It is the
mode-resolved component of the per-antenna quantity [launched power of a
lower-hybrid antenna](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

The joint power density is defined by

$$
S(n_{\mathrm{tor}},n_{\mathrm{pol}}) = \frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}P_{\mathrm{launched}}}{\mathrm{d}n_{\mathrm{tor}}\,\mathrm{d}n_{\mathrm{pol}}}
$$

where $S$ is the launched-power density over the two refractive-index
coordinates, $P_{\mathrm{launched}}$ is the net launched power of the
antenna, $n_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal component of the lower-hybrid
wave refractive-index vector, and $n_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is its poloidal
component. These components correspond to the [toroidal launched wave index
of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:toroidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and
[poloidal launched wave index of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:poloidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna); they
are refractive-index coordinates rather than integer Fourier harmonic
numbers.

The quantity applies to one selected lower-hybrid antenna row at a given
time. It is resolved over both refractive-index coordinates, is not
aggregated over antenna rows or antennas, and is not a time average.

Because the underlying launched power is net power after accounting for
reflected power, this quantity is distinct from [forward power of a
lower-hybrid antenna](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and
[reflected power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). It represents power
entering the vacuum vessel, not generator output, incident forward power,
returning reflected power, or power absorbed by the plasma.

Integrating $S$ over $n_{\mathrm{tor}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{pol}}$ recovers the
corresponding [launched power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna), while integrating
over $n_{\mathrm{pol}}$ gives the [per-toroidal-mode launched power of a
lower-hybrid
antenna](name:per_toroidal_mode_launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

sources.parent_definition: Set of horizontal rows of waveguides (corresponding to different poloidal positions). A power spectrum is provided for each row.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna resolved per unit toroidal
refractive-index interval is the net lower-hybrid wave-power distribution
from one selected antenna row.
NAMES.long:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna resolved per unit toroidal
refractive-index interval is the distribution of net RF power entering the
vacuum vessel over the toroidal refractive-index variable for one selected
antenna row. It is the toroidal-resolved component of the per-antenna
launched-power quantity represented by [launched power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

The distribution is defined by the differential power relation:

$$
\frac{dP_{\mathrm{launched}}}{dn_{\mathrm{tor}}}
= \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{launched}}(n_{\mathrm{tor}})
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{launched}}$ is the total net RF power launched by the
selected antenna, $n_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the signed toroidal component of the
lower-hybrid wave refractive-index vector, and
$\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{launched}}$ is the launched-power density with respect
to the toroidal refractive-index interval.

The quantity applies to one selected lower-hybrid antenna row and is
resolved only over the toroidal refractive-index coordinate; it is not
aggregated over multiple antenna rows, antennas, or toroidal
refractive-index intervals. The coordinate $n_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the
toroidal wave index identified by [toroidal launched wave index of a
lower-hybrid
antenna](name:toroidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

It denotes net power entering the vacuum vessel after reflected power is
subtracted from incident forward power. It is distinct from [reflected power
of a lower-hybrid antenna](name:reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna),
generator output, and [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power), which
describes power transferred to the plasma rather than power launched from
the antenna.

Integrating this distribution over the supported range of $n_{\mathrm{tor}}$
recovers the per-antenna quantity [launched power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). The corresponding
[per toroidal and poloidal mode number launched power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:per_toroidal_and_poloidal_mode_number_launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna)
resolves the same launched-power distribution over both toroidal and
poloidal refractive-index intervals.

sources.parent_definition: Set of horizontal rows of waveguides (corresponding to different poloidal positions). A power spectrum is provided for each row.

NAMES.name: power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short:
Net ion-cyclotron radio-frequency power launched through a heating antenna
into the vacuum vessel, equal to forward power minus reflected power at the
antenna boundary.
NAMES.long:
Net ion-cyclotron radio-frequency power is the power delivered through an
ion-cyclotron heating antenna into the vacuum vessel toward the plasma. It
is a launcher-boundary quantity, not the generator output or the power
ultimately absorbed by plasma particles.

The defining net-power relation is:

$$
P_{\rm net}=P_{\rm forward}-P_{\rm reflected}
$$

where $P_{\rm net}$ is the net ion-cyclotron power launched toward the
plasma, $P_{\rm forward}$ is the incident radio-frequency power traveling
toward the antenna as described by [forward power of an ion-cyclotron
heating antenna](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and
$P_{\rm reflected}$ is the radio-frequency power returned from the antenna
toward the source.

At launcher resolution, the quantity applies to a specified ion-cyclotron
heating antenna and has no species, charge-state, or volumetric deposition
resolution. The unqualified form represents the launcher-associated value;
the system-level aggregation is represented separately by [total power due
to ion-cyclotron heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating).

Reflected power and losses upstream of the antenna boundary are excluded.
The quantity therefore describes power launched toward the plasma rather
than forward incident power before reflection or the fraction subsequently
absorbed by plasma particles. The total-power variant is obtained by summing
the corresponding launcher-resolved values over all ion-cyclotron heating
antennas, while [launched power of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) provides the
antenna-oriented expression of the same net boundary power.

NAMES.name: pressure_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Pressure associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module,
representing mechanical normal loading or contained-gas pressure at hardware
components.
NAMES.long:
Pressure associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module represents
the compressive normal stress or contained-gas pressure acting at its
hardware components.

At a surface, pressure is defined as the normal force distributed over the
loaded area:

$$
p = \frac{F_n}{A}
$$

where $p$ is pressure, $F_n$ is the force normal to the surface, and $A$ is
the area over which that force acts. For contained gas, the same scalar
represents the isotropic normal stress exerted by the gas.

The scope is the antenna module and its associated hardware components,
including local mechanical or gas-pressure conditions at individual sensing
locations. The quantity is not a plasma pressure, a pressure amplitude, a
pressure variation, or an aggregate sum or average over the module.

Pressure is a mechanical or fluid-state property and is independent of
electrical properties such as the antenna's
[resistance](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and [strap
current](name:current_of_antenna_strap).

NAMES.name: radial_outline_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate of each point on an antenna-strap outline in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity gives the major-radius coordinate of a point on the geometric
outline of an antenna strap. It identifies the point's perpendicular
distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The quantity is pointwise and unaggregated over the antenna-strap outline:
each value applies to one outline point. It does not represent the strap's
reference-point coordinate, center coordinate, radial extent, or
outer-radius bound.

The complementary [toroidal angle of the antenna
strap](name:toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap) specifies the angular location
of the same outline point. The [radial coordinate of the antenna
strap](name:radial_coordinate_of_antenna_strap) instead locates a specified
strap geometry reference point and is therefore not interchangeable with
this outline coordinate.

NAMES.name: reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Relative phase angle of a reflected radio-frequency power-wave phasor at an
antenna element in an ion-cyclotron heating launcher, measured relative to
the forward power-wave phasor of that same element.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the relative phase of a complex reflected radio-frequency
power-wave phasor at a selected antenna strap or module with respect to the
complex forward radio-frequency power-wave phasor of the same strap or
module. It specifies the element-local reflection phase of an ion-cyclotron
heating launcher rather than an absolute phase or an inter-element phase.

For element $i$, the reflected phase is defined by

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{ref},i} = \arg\!\left(b_i^{\mathrm{ref}} (a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}})^*\right) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $\phi_{\mathrm{ref},i}$ is this reflected phase, $b_i^{\mathrm{ref}}$
is the complex reflected power-wave phasor at element $i$,
$a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the complex forward power-wave phasor at the same
element, $(a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}})^*$ is its complex conjugate, and $\arg$
extracts the phase angle. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$.

The scope is a single selected launcher strap or module and the pair of
forward and reflected traveling power waves at the same element reference
plane. The forward wave propagates toward the antenna element, and the
reflected wave propagates away from the antenna element toward the feeding
network. The first launcher element is not the phase reference for this
quantity, and the quantity is not averaged or summed over launcher elements.

This quantity is a reflected-wave member of the broader [phase of the
ion-cyclotron heating antenna] family. It is distinct from the [wave phase
of the ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), which describes
inter-element phasing, and together with the [reflected power of the
ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) it specifies
the phase-and-magnitude state of the reflected power wave without including
the magnitude itself.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the reflected-wave phasor at the selected
element leads the forward-wave phasor at the same element in phase under the
adopted temporal phasor convention.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the reflected power with respect to the forward power of this module
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

NAMES.name: reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Reflected power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the
backward-traveling radio-frequency power returned from one antenna toward
the transmission-line source rather than coupled into the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Reflected power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the
backward-traveling radio-frequency wave power at a defined reference plane
on the feed line, directed away from the antenna toward the source. It is
the returned component of the antenna-associated power and represents
incident power rejected by antenna-plasma coupling.

At a common reference plane, the reflected and forward traveling-wave powers
are related by

$$
P_{\mathrm{ref}} = |\Gamma|^2 P_{\mathrm{fwd}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reflected power, $\Gamma$ is the complex
wave reflection coefficient, and $P_{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the [forward
power](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) traveling toward
the antenna.

This quantity applies to one ion-cyclotron heating antenna and represents
the aggregate returned power associated with that antenna at the defined
reference plane. When an antenna contains multiple modules, it is distinct
from reflected power assigned to an individual module; it also excludes
forward power, power coupled into the plasma, and source power not present
at the reference plane.

It complements [forward
power](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) as the opposite
traveling-wave component at the feed-line reference plane. The [launched
power] is power delivered from the antenna into the plasma, so it is
physically distinct from returned reflected power; the two quantities must
not be identified or substituted for one another.

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Toroidal angular coordinate of each antenna-strap outline point around the
machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal angle is the azimuthal coordinate assigned to each point on the
geometric outline of an antenna strap. It identifies the point’s
circumferential location in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies to individual strap-outline points and is not a mean,
sum, nominal center coordinate, or mechanical orientation angle. No
aggregation over the outline is implied; each point retains its own $\phi$
value.

Together with the other coordinates of the outline, this angle locates the
strap geometry. It is distinct from the [radial coordinate of the antenna
strap](name:radial_coordinate_of_antenna_strap), which locates a strap
reference point, while [vertical outline of the antenna
strap](name:vertical_outline_of_antenna_strap) provides the corresponding
signed vertical coordinate for outline points. The same angular-coordinate
concept is used for a different object by [toroidal angle of a coil
conductor element](name:toroidal_angle_of_coil_conductor_element).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the angular displacement from the chosen
$\phi=0$ reference is toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+Z$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle (oriented counter-clockwise when viewing from above)
sources.parent_definition: Strap outline

NAMES.name: total_external_heating_power
NAMES.short:
Total non-inductive power coupled from external neutral-beam and
radio-frequency heating systems to the plasma, summed over auxiliary sources
and excluding Ohmic heating.
NAMES.long:
Total external heating power is the aggregate non-inductive power coupled to
the plasma by auxiliary heating systems. It includes neutral-beam injection
and electron-cyclotron, ion-cyclotron, and lower-hybrid systems, while
excluding power associated with Ohmic induction.

The defining aggregate relation is

$$
P_{\mathrm{ext}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aux}}} P_s
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the total external heating power,
$\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is the set of included auxiliary heating
systems, and $P_s$ is the power coupled to the plasma by auxiliary source
$s$.

The quantity applies to the whole plasma and is summed over all included
auxiliary sources rather than resolved by source, species, or spatial
region. It represents external power input that may contribute to both
plasma heating and non-inductive current drive; it is distinct from Ohmic
heating and from generator power that is not coupled to the plasma.
Source-specific contributions include [total power due to electron-cyclotron
heating](name:total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating), [total power
due to ion-cyclotron
heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating), and power absorbed
from a [neutral-beam
injector](name:absorbed_power_of_neutral_beam_injector), whose aggregate
forms contribute to the sum.

NAMES.name: total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short:
Total ion-cyclotron radio-frequency power launched into the vacuum vessel by
the complete heating-antenna system, summed over all antennas.
NAMES.long:
Total ion-cyclotron radio-frequency power is the aggregate power launched
into the vacuum vessel by the complete ion-cyclotron heating-antenna system.
It represents the net launcher-array power directed toward the plasma,
rather than power ultimately absorbed by plasma particles.

The system total is defined by summing the launched power from each antenna:

$$
P_{\rm total}=\sum_{i=1}^{N_{\rm ant}} P_i
$$

where $P_{\rm total}$ is the total ion-cyclotron radio-frequency power
launched by the system, $N_{\rm ant}$ is the number of contributing
ion-cyclotron heating antennas, $i$ is an antenna index, and $P_i$ is the
net power launched by antenna $i$, corresponding to the antenna-resolved
[ion-cyclotron heating power](name:power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating).

The quantity applies to the complete heating system and is aggregated over
all ion-cyclotron heating antennas. It has no individual-antenna, species,
charge-state, or volumetric deposition resolution. Reflected power and
losses upstream of the vacuum-vessel launch boundary are excluded, and the
quantity does not represent the portion subsequently absorbed by plasma
particles.

This system-level total is the aggregate counterpart of [launched power due
to ion-cyclotron heating](name:launched_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating),
while [launched power of an ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) represents
the corresponding launcher-oriented power for an individual antenna.

sources.parent_definition: Antenna systems for heating and current drive in the ion cyclotron (IC) frequencies.

NAMES.name: vertical_outline_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Signed vertical coordinate of each contour point defining an ion-cyclotron
antenna strap boundary, distinguishing the strap outline from its
geometric-center location.
NAMES.long:
The vertical outline coordinate is the signed height of one contour point on
the geometric boundary of an ion-cyclotron antenna strap, expressed in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It describes boundary
geometry rather than a field or thermodynamic quantity.

The quantity applies pointwise to the strap outline: each value belongs to
one boundary contour point. Values are not summed, averaged, or integrated
over the outline, and the quantity does not represent the strap's
geometric-center location.

The geometric-center location is represented separately by the [vertical
coordinate of the antenna strap](name:vertical_coordinate_of_antenna_strap).
Collectively, the coordinates of corresponding outline points define the
strap boundary geometry.

NAMES.name: voltage_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Voltage of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna is the electrical potential
difference across an ordered pair of antenna feed terminals or reference
points. Its polarity is set by that ordering; amplitude specializations
represent the magnitude of the radio-frequency voltage waveform.
NAMES.long:
Voltage of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna is the electrical potential
difference across an ordered pair of feed terminals or reference points
belonging to an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna. It denotes the antenna
feed-terminal voltage quantity itself, not a generic circuit voltage
detached from the antenna feed system.

For an ordered terminal or reference-point pair $(a,b)$, the voltage is
defined by the potential difference:

$$
V_{ab} = \Phi_a - \Phi_b
$$

where $V_{ab}$ is the voltage of the ion-cyclotron-heating antenna for the
ordered pair $(a,b)$, and $\Phi_a$ and $\Phi_b$ are the electric potentials
at the first and second members of that pair.

This parent quantity covers antenna feed-terminal voltage representations
for ion-cyclotron-heating antennas, including signed potential differences
and magnitude-only specializations. It excludes quantities whose primary
identity is generator voltage, transmission-line current, delivered power,
reflected power, or plasma potential rather than the antenna feed-terminal
voltage.

The [voltage amplitude of an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:voltage_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna_amplitude) is a
specialization of this quantity that reports the peak magnitude of the
radio-frequency voltage waveform on an antenna feed; as an amplitude, it
does not carry the terminal-order sign of $V_{ab}$.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the electric potential at the first terminal
or reference point of the ordered ion-cyclotron-heating antenna pair is
greater than that at the second.

NAMES.name: voltage_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna_amplitude
NAMES.short:
Peak magnitude of the radio-frequency voltage signal on one
transmission-line feed of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module, used in
feed power and reflection analysis.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the peak radio-frequency voltage amplitude associated with
one transmission-line feed serving one ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module.
It represents the magnitude of the oscillating feed voltage rather than its
instantaneous signed value or phase.

For a voltage waveform, the peak amplitude is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{amp}} = \max_t |V(t)|
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is the peak voltage amplitude, $V(t)$ is the
instantaneous signed voltage between the ordered feed terminals, and $t$ is
time.

The quantity applies to a single transmission-line feed of a single antenna
module. It is not a module-averaged or antenna-system-aggregated voltage,
and it excludes the instantaneous waveform and phase information represented
by the underlying [voltage of the ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:voltage_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna).

The amplitude is the magnitude transformation of that parent voltage
quantity: the parent defines the terminal potential difference, while this
quantity retains its peak magnitude for radio-frequency power and reflection
analysis. It is distinct from reflected power, which characterizes returned
wave energy rather than feed voltage.

sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of voltage measurements

NAMES.name: wave_current_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Radio-frequency electric current carried along an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna strap during electromagnetic-wave excitation, including
instantaneous, peak, and root-mean-square representations.
NAMES.long:
Wave current of an antenna strap is the directed conventional electric
charge flow in the conducting strap associated specifically with
electromagnetic-wave excitation. It is a vector quantity whose direction
follows charge transport along the strap, while its magnitude may vary with
strap position and excitation phase.

The directed current is represented by

$$
\mathbf{I}(t)=\frac{dQ(t)}{dt}\,\hat{\ell}
$$

where $\mathbf{I}(t)$ is the vector current, $Q(t)$ is the conventional
electric charge that has crossed a reference strap cross-section, $t$ is
time, and $\hat{\ell}$ is the positive unit tangent along the strap.

This quantity is restricted to the wave-excitation contribution in the
conducting antenna strap. No temporal averaging, peak extraction, or
magnitude operation is intrinsic to the parent quantity; the physical region
is the antenna strap itself, and the charge flow is treated as a directed
current rather than an aggregate plasma-current contribution.

The parent specializes the broader [current of an antenna
strap](name:current_of_antenna_strap) by identifying the component
associated with electromagnetic-wave excitation. The [root-mean-square wave
current of an antenna
strap](name:root_mean_square_of_wave_current_of_antenna_strap) is its
non-negative effective temporal value, whereas [wave current of an antenna
strap amplitude](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap_amplitude) is its peak
magnitude at a specified strap location. These representations are distinct
from plasma current generated by wave–particle interactions, such as
[current due to wave-driven current
drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive). For a sinusoidal
current, the scalar RMS and peak magnitudes satisfy
$I_{\mathrm{rms}}=I_{\mathrm{pk}}/\sqrt{2}$, where $I_{\mathrm{rms}}$ is the
RMS current magnitude and $I_{\mathrm{pk}}$ is the peak current magnitude.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when conventional charge flow follows the defined
positive tangent direction along the antenna strap.

NAMES.name: root_mean_square_of_wave_current_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Effective non-negative magnitude of the radio-frequency current oscillating
along a single ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap.
NAMES.long:
The root-mean-square wave current is the effective magnitude of the
oscillatory radio-frequency current carried by one ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna strap during wave excitation. It is a non-negative scalar that
represents the current waveform over an RF cycle.

For an RF period, the RMS current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{RMS}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{T_{\mathrm{RF}}}\int_{0}^{T_{\mathrm{RF}}} i^2(t)\,dt}
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{RMS}}$ is the RMS wave current, $i(t)$ is the
instantaneous wave current in the strap, $t$ is time, and $T_{\mathrm{RF}}$
is the RF period. The time origin is arbitrary within the period.

The quantity applies to a single antenna strap and averages over one RF
period; it is not a sum over straps or antenna modules. It describes the
strap-conductor current associated with the launched wave and excludes
plasma current and non-wave direct current.

It is the RMS transformation of the underlying [wave current of antenna
strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap). Unlike that parent quantity, it
does not retain instantaneous sign or phase. For sinusoidal excitation, it
equals the peak current magnitude divided by the square root of two and
therefore differs from the [wave current of antenna strap
amplitude](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap_amplitude).

sources.leaf_definition: Root mean square current flowing along the strap
sources.parent_definition: Set of IC antenna straps

NAMES.name: wave_current_of_antenna_strap_amplitude
NAMES.short:
Peak magnitude of the radio-frequency current oscillating along an
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap at a specified location.
NAMES.long:
The strap-current amplitude is the non-negative peak magnitude of the
radio-frequency current associated with electromagnetic-wave excitation at a
specified location along an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap.

For the oscillatory current represented by a complex phasor, the amplitude
is defined as

$$
I_{\mathrm{amp}} = |\widetilde{I}|
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is the strap-current amplitude and $\widetilde{I}$
is the complex phasor of the strap current at the specified location.

This quantity applies to one antenna strap within one antenna module and is
evaluated at the relevant position along that strap. It characterizes the
radio-frequency excitation associated with the module's wave current; it is
not summed or averaged over multiple straps, modules, or the complete
antenna system. The amplitude is non-negative and therefore excludes the
sign and phase information of the instantaneous current.

As the amplitude form of [wave current of antenna
strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap), it retains the parent quantity's
strap locus and wave-current meaning while selecting its peak magnitude. It
is distinct from the instantaneous signed current and from a
root-mean-square representation of the same oscillatory current.

sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of current measurements

NAMES.name: wave_phase_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Phase angle of the radio-frequency current phasor carried by one
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap, defined relative to a specified RF
phase reference.
NAMES.long:
Wave phase of an antenna strap is the phase angle of the oscillatory
radio-frequency current phasor carried by that strap. It describes the
strap-level excitation phase used in the antenna's toroidal phasing
configuration.

The complex strap-current phasor may be represented as

$$
I_s = |I_s|e^{i\phi_s}
$$

where $I_s$ is the complex radio-frequency current phasor, $|I_s|$ is its
current amplitude, and $\phi_s$ is the wave phase represented by this
quantity. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$ relative to a specified RF
reference phase.

This quantity applies to one antenna strap and is not summed or averaged
over multiple straps. It refers to the phase of the strap current, not the
phase of a forward power-wave phasor, which is represented by [forward wave
phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), or the
phase associated with a complete antenna element.

The associated [wave current of antenna
strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap) provides the phasor whose phase
is specified, while [wave current of antenna strap
amplitude](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap_amplitude) determines its
magnitude rather than its phase. Relative phases between straps determine
the toroidal phasing of the antenna excitation and therefore influence the
launched wave excitation spectrum. The phase-reference plane and any
phase-unwrapping convention must be specified separately when comparing
values.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the strap current
sources.parent_definition: Set of IC antenna straps

NAMES.name: wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Relative phase angle of a radio-frequency phasor at an antenna element in an
ion-cyclotron heating launcher, measured relative to the first element for
inter-element phasing.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the relative phase of a complex radio-frequency phasor at a
selected antenna strap or module feed with respect to the first reference
element. It specifies inter-element phasing of an ion-cyclotron heating
launcher rather than an absolute phase.

For selected element $i$, the relative phase is defined by

$$
\Delta\phi_i = \arg\left(A_i A_1^*\right) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $\Delta\phi_i$ is the relative phase of element $i$, $A_i$ is its
complex radio-frequency voltage or wave phasor, $A_1$ is the phasor of the
first reference element, $A_1^*$ is the complex conjugate of that reference
phasor, and $\arg$ extracts the phase angle. The reference element has zero
relative phase, and the result is defined modulo $2\pi$.

The quantity applies independently to one selected antenna element or module
feed and is not summed or averaged over modules. It describes the
radio-frequency signal associated with the antenna feed, not a phase
belonging to a plasma population or integrated over a plasma region. It
excludes absolute phase, amplitude, power, and reflection coefficient,
although the phase may characterize a complex feed voltage or traveling-wave
quantity.

The family parent [phase of the ion-cyclotron heating antenna] provides the
common relative-phase meaning. Propagation-specific instances retain this
definition while selecting the wave direction, as in the [forward wave phase
of the ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and the
[reflected phase of the ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected element's radio-frequency phasor
leads the first reference element in phase under the adopted temporal phasor
convention.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of voltage measurements

NAMES.name: forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short:
Relative phase of the forward radio-frequency power-wave phasor at an
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module, referenced to the first module for
inter-module toroidal phasing.
NAMES.long:
The forward-wave phase is the relative phase angle of the complex
radio-frequency power-wave phasor associated with one ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna module. It describes inter-module phasing rather than an absolute
phase.

For selected module $i$, the relative forward-wave phase is defined by

$$
\theta_i^{+} = \arg\left(\tilde{a}_i^{+}\right) - \arg\left(\tilde{a}_1^{+}\right)
$$

where $\theta_i^{+}$ is the relative forward-wave phase, $i$ identifies the
selected antenna module, module $1$ is the first reference module,
$\tilde{a}_i^{+}$ is the complex phasor of the forward radio-frequency power
wave associated with module $i$, and $\arg$ returns a phasor's phase angle.

The quantity applies only to the forward wave at an antenna module and is
defined relative to the first module; no absolute phase relative to a
generator or external reference is implied. It concerns the electromagnetic
power-wave phasor, not a plasma-particle quantity or a spatially distributed
plasma field.

This is the forward-wave specialization of the relative antenna phasor phase
defined by [wave phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna). It is distinct
from the relative phase of the reflected wave, [reflected phase of an
ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and from
the phase of the RF current carried by an antenna strap, [wave phase of an
antenna strap](name:wave_phase_of_antenna_strap).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the selected module's forward-wave phasor
leads the first reference module in phase.

sources.leaf_definition: Phase of the forward power with respect to the first module
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate locating the antenna strap’s specified geometry
reference point in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The antenna-strap radial coordinate is the major-radius position of the
strap’s specified geometry reference point, measured from the toroidal
symmetry axis. It identifies the strap location in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, rather than describing the strap’s
orientation or extent.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, and $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal
Cartesian coordinates of the reference point relative to the toroidal
symmetry axis in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
basis.

This quantity applies to the antenna strap reference point only; it is not
averaged over the strap length, thickness, or cross-section, and it does not
denote a flux-surface-normal projection. It is the antenna-strap-specific
realization of [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate). The
corresponding [toroidal angle of the antenna
strap](name:toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap) and [vertical coordinate of the
antenna strap](name:vertical_coordinate_of_antenna_strap) provide
complementary cylindrical location coordinates.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate locating the sphere center that defines an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the major-radius coordinate $R$ of the center of the sphere
that defines an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror. It identifies the
mirror's geometric reference point rather than a point on the reflecting
surface.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the major-radius
coordinate relates to right-handed Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ through

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian
coordinate values in the $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies to the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's spherical
defining geometry and represents one geometric point. It is not a plasma
quantity, a surface coordinate, a mirror steering angle, or an average or
integral over the mirror.

The broader [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) concept is
specialized here to the sphere center of the mirror. Together with the
[vertical coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror](name:vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and
[toroidal coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), it
locates the same geometric center.

sources.leaf_definition: Major radius
sources.parent_definition: Position of the center of the sphere which defines the mirror, in the case of a spherical mirror (geometry_type = 2), derived from the above geometric data

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_launching_position
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate locating the electron-cyclotron beam launching
position relative to the toroidal symmetry axis.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the major-radius coordinate of the position at which an
electron-cyclotron beam is launched, locating that position by its
perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.

The coordinate is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame by

$$
R_{\mathrm{launch}} = \sqrt{x_{\mathrm{launch}}^2 + y_{\mathrm{launch}}^2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{launch}}$ is the major-radius coordinate of the launching
position, and $x_{\mathrm{launch}}$ and $y_{\mathrm{launch}}$ are its
Cartesian coordinates in the plane perpendicular to the toroidal symmetry
axis. In the cylindrical frame, $R$ denotes major radius, $\phi$ denotes
toroidal angle, and $Z$ denotes vertical coordinate.

The quantity applies specifically to the electron-cyclotron beam launching
position and represents one geometric coordinate without averaging or
aggregation over positions, beams, or launchers.

It specifies only the major-radius coordinate; it does not represent the
toroidal-angle or vertical coordinate of the launching position and is
distinct from the radial coordinate of an extended launcher component or
mirror.

This quantity is the launching-position specialization of the general
[radial_coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), with the evaluation locus fixed
to the beam launching position. It differs from
[radial_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror](name:radial_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror),
which locates the geometric center of a launcher mirror.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate of the neutral beam injector center, measured from
the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial coordinate of a neutral beam injector is the major-radius
location of the injector unit center relative to the toroidal symmetry axis.
It is a nonnegative geometric coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the injector center, the radial coordinate is related to its Cartesian
coordinates by

$$
R = \\sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates of the same
injector center in the right-handed Cartesian $(\\hat{x},\\hat{y},\\hat{z})$
basis.

This quantity applies to one selected neutral beam injector unit and
represents the unit-center position only. It is not an aggregate over
multiple injectors and does not represent a beam trajectory, launch point,
deposition location, or plasma response.

It is the neutral-beam-injector specialization of the general [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), with the geometric point fixed to the
injector unit center.

sources.parent_definition: Major radius

NAMES.name: density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Local number density of a specified plasma species or species group
immediately upstream of a divertor-target sheath, with ion charge states
summed and neutral populations excluded unless explicitly named.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the local particle count per volume for a selected plasma
species or species group at the plasma-facing side of a divertor target. It
is evaluated immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath, rather than
in the target material or as a quantity integrated over a target surface.

For a selected set of constituent populations, the number density is defined
by:

$$
n_S = \sum_{s \in S} n_s
$$

where $n_S$ is the number density of the selected species or species group,
$S$ is the set of included constituent populations, and $n_s$ is the number
density of constituent population $s$.

The selected population can be free electrons, one ion species, or a named
group of ion species such as deuterium and tritium. For an ion species, $S$
contains its positive atomic charge states and the sum is an unweighted
particle-count sum; for a compound fuel group, it contains the included
isotope ions. Neutral atoms and molecules are excluded unless explicitly
named as part of $S$. The quantity is local to the plasma immediately
upstream of one divertor-target sheath and is neither a target-surface
integral nor an aggregation over multiple targets.

Species-specific instances refine this common definition, including
[electron density at the divertor
target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), [boron density at the
divertor target](name:boron_density_at_divertor_target), and
[deuterium-tritium density at the divertor
target](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target). In contrast,
[total ion number density at the plasma
boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) sums all charged ion
species at a plasma boundary, making it broader in species scope and
distinct in locus.

NAMES.name: argon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short:
Number density of argon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance, summed over positive ionization
states and excluding neutral argon.
NAMES.long:
Number density of argon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the argon-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The charge-state-summed argon number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the total argon-ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the local number density of argon ions with
positive charge state $q$, and $q$ is the integer argon charge-state index.

This quantity applies to the argon-ion population immediately upstream of
the electrostatic sheath at a divertor target and is summed over all
positive argon charge states from singly ionized through fully stripped
argon. Neutral argon atoms and other neutral argon forms are excluded, as
are electrons and ions of other elements.

This is a local species density rather than a density integrated over the
target surface or summed over all plasma species. The corresponding argon
quantity at a limiter, [argon density at the
limiter](name:argon_density_at_limiter), has the same charge-state
aggregation but a different evaluation locus; unlike [electron density at
the divertor target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), this
quantity describes argon ions rather than free electrons.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: beryllium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Number density of beryllium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary, summed over all positive ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of beryllium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the beryllium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local beryllium-ion number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Be}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium-ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the number of beryllium ions in the volume, and $V$ is
a small plasma volume centered at the sheath entrance.

This quantity applies to the ionized beryllium population immediately
adjacent to the divertor target and is summed over all positive beryllium
ionization states, with each ion counted once regardless of charge state.
Neutral beryllium atoms are excluded; the quantity is a local number
density, not an areal particle flux, integrated inventory, or charge
density.

Compared with [beryllium_density](name:beryllium_density), this quantity
specifies the divertor-target sheath-entrance locus. It is distinct from
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target),
which counts free electrons rather than beryllium ions.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: boron_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short:
Boron density at the divertor target is the local number density of boron
ions immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath at the target-facing
plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Boron density at the divertor target is the local number density of boron
ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to the divertor target surface,
evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the
boron-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The charge-state-summed boron ion density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{B}} = \sum_{q=1}^{5} n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the boron ion number density and
$n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}$ is the number density of boron ions with positive
charge state $q$.

This quantity applies to the boron-ion population immediately upstream of
the sheath at a divertor target and aggregates all positive boron ionization
states, from singly ionized through fully stripped boron. Each boron ion is
counted once; neutral boron atoms are excluded.

Relative to the parent
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target), this quantity
selects boron ions rather than an unspecified species or species group. It
is parallel to
[beryllium_density_at_divertor_target](name:beryllium_density_at_divertor_target),
differing in the selected ion species and its allowed charge states.

sources.parent_definition: Boron (B)

NAMES.name: carbon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Number density of the carbon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for carbon ions at the sheath entrance immediately
upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the carbon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the carbon-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local carbon-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{C}^{+}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{C}^{+}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{C}^{+}}$ is the carbon-ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{C}^{+}}$ is the number of carbon ions in all positive ionization
states, and $V$ is a small plasma volume whose center approaches the sheath
entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to carbon ions immediately upstream of the
electrostatic sheath at a divertor target and is summed over all positive
carbon ionization states, from singly ionized through fully stripped carbon.
Neutral carbon atoms, carbon-bearing neutral molecules, electrons, and ions
of other elements are excluded.

Unlike [carbon_density](name:carbon_density), which has the broader
elemental-carbon scope including neutral carbon, this quantity is restricted
to the charge-state-summed positive-ion population at the divertor target.

NAMES.name: deuterium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Number density of deuterium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of deuterium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the deuterium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local deuterium number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_D = \frac{dN_D}{dV}
$$

where $N_D$ is the number of deuterium ions in a small plasma volume $V$
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the deuterium-ion population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and is summed over all positive atomic deuterium
ionization states, counting each ion once regardless of charge state.
Neutral deuterium atoms and molecules, electrons, and ions of other species
are excluded.

Unlike
[deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target),
which includes both fuel-ion species, this quantity contains deuterium ions
only. It is the divertor-target-localized counterpart of
[deuterium_density](name:deuterium_density).

sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species at
the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the
plasma-side sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species at the
divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath
entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is
the deuterium-tritium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local deuterium-tritium number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_{DT} = \frac{dN_{DT}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{DT}$ is the number of particles represented by the effective
deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species, and $V$ is a small plasma volume
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the ion population represented as one effective
deuterium-tritium fuel species, rather than to separately resolved deuterium
and tritium populations. It includes the positive ionic states represented
by that pseudo-species and excludes neutral deuterium-tritium atoms or
molecules, electrons, and other ion species.

The localized quantity is the divertor-target counterpart of
[deuterium_tritium_density](name:deuterium_tritium_density). Unlike
[deuterium_density_at_divertor_target](name:deuterium_density_at_divertor_target)
and
[tritium_density_at_divertor_target](name:tritium_density_at_divertor_target),
which describe the separately resolved isotope populations, this quantity
uses the prescribed effective deuterium-tritium pseudo-species.

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of the electron species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for free electrons at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the electron species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the electron-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local electron number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_e = \frac{dN_e}{dV}
$$

where $N_e$ is the number of free electrons in a small plasma volume $V$
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the free-electron population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and counts each free electron once, without
charge-state weighting. Electrons bound in atoms or molecules, ions, and
other neutral particles are excluded.

Unlike
[total_ion_density_at_divertor_target](name:total_ion_density_at_divertor_target),
which sums positive-ion densities over ion species and charge states, this
quantity describes the electron population and is not an ionic density or a
charge density.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Local rate of energy deposition per unit divertor-target area, combining all
incident particle and radiative energy-carrying channels.
NAMES.long:
Energy flux at a divertor target is the local surface density of power
deposited by incident plasma and radiative energy carriers on the
target-facing surface. It describes the energy load at each surface location
rather than power integrated over a target or divertor assembly.

The local energy flux is defined by

$$
q_E(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{\mathrm{d}P_E}{\mathrm{d}A}
$$

where $q_E(\mathbf{x})$ is the deposited energy flux at surface position
$\mathbf{x}$, $P_E$ is the cumulative deposited power from all included
incident energy carriers, and $A$ is target-surface area.

The quantity applies to one divertor target surface and combines the
contributions of incident particle and radiative energy channels. It does
not resolve separate electron, ion, conductive, convective,
neutral-particle, or radiative contributions, and it is not a
target-integrated power.

This quantity is the energy-deposition component represented by [flux at a
divertor target](name:flux_at_divertor_target); the latter provides the
carrier-independent target-surface load. The corresponding surface maximum,
[maximum of energy flux at a divertor
target](name:maximum_of_energy_flux_at_divertor_target), is obtained by
selecting the largest value of $q_E(\mathbf{x})$ over the target surface.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary, summed over positive ionization states and
excluding neutral helium-3 atoms.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the helium-3-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local helium-3 number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_3 = \frac{dN_3}{dV}
$$

where $n_3$ is the helium-3 ion number density, $N_3$ is the number of
helium-3 ions in a small plasma volume, and $V$ is that plasma volume. The
count $N_3$ includes singly ionized and fully stripped helium-3 ions.

This quantity applies to the helium-3 ion population immediately upstream of
the electrostatic sheath at a divertor target. It is summed over the
positive ionization states of helium-3, excludes neutral helium-3 atoms, and
excludes electrons and all other ion species.

Unlike
[helium_4_density_at_divertor_target](name:helium_4_density_at_divertor_target),
this quantity describes the isotope with three nucleons. Unlike
[helium_3_density_at_limiter](name:helium_3_density_at_limiter), it is
evaluated at a divertor target rather than at a limiter surface.

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance, summed over singly and doubly
ionized states and excluding neutral helium-4.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the helium-4-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The helium-4 ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{He4}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the number of helium-4 ions, and $V$ is a small plasma
volume whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to the ionized helium-4 population immediately
adjacent to the divertor target and is summed over the singly and doubly
ionized charge states, with each ion counted once. Neutral helium-4 atoms
are excluded, so this quantity is not the total helium-4 particle density
including neutrals or a charge density.

As a species-specific specialization, this quantity contributes to the
broader [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) family
without including other ion species. The isotope distinction from
[helium_3_density_at_divertor_target](name:helium_3_density_at_divertor_target)
is maintained; the two quantities describe different helium isotopes.

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of the hydrogen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for hydrogen ions at the sheath entrance, summed
over positive charge states and excluding neutral hydrogen atoms and
molecules.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the hydrogen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the hydrogen-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local hydrogen-ion number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{H}}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the number of free hydrogen ions in a small plasma
volume $V$ whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side
at the divertor target, and $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the corresponding local
hydrogen-ion number density.

This quantity applies to the free hydrogen-ion population immediately
adjacent to the divertor target. It is summed over all positive hydrogen
ionization charge states, counting each ion once without charge weighting;
neutral hydrogen atoms and molecules, electrons, and other ion species are
excluded.

As a species-specific local component, it uses the same sheath-entrance
locus and charge-state-summed convention as [deuterium density at the
divertor target](name:deuterium_density_at_divertor_target), but represents
hydrogen ions rather than deuterium ions. Unlike the flux-surface-averaged
[hydrogen density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary),
it is evaluated locally at the divertor target rather than averaged over a
flux surface.

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Number density of the iron species at the divertor target is the particle
count per volume for iron ions at the sheath entrance immediately upstream
of the target-facing plasma boundary. Positive charge states are summed;
neutral iron is excluded.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the iron species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the iron-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local iron-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron-ion number density, $\mathrm{Fe}$
denotes iron, $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the number of free iron ions, and $V$ is
a small plasma volume whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the
plasma side.

This quantity applies to the free iron-ion population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and is summed over all positive iron charge states,
counting each iron ion once without charge-state weighting. Neutral iron
atoms, electrons, other ion species, and charge density are excluded.

It is a species-resolved component of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target), whereas
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target)
describes the free-electron population and
[carbon_density_at_divertor_target](name:carbon_density_at_divertor_target)
applies the same target-locus and charge-state-summed convention to carbon
ions.

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Number density of the krypton species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for krypton ions at the sheath entrance, summed
over positive ionization states and excluding neutral krypton atoms.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the krypton species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for krypton ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the
krypton-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local krypton-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Kr}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton-ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{Kr}}$
is the number of krypton ions, and $V$ is the local plasma volume.

This quantity applies to the krypton-ion population immediately adjacent to
a divertor target, evaluated at the plasma-side entrance to the
electrostatic sheath. It is summed over all positive krypton ionization
states, counting each ion once; neutral krypton atoms, electrons, and ions
of other species are excluded.

As a species-specific target-locus quantity, it specializes the broader
[krypton_density](name:krypton_density) by restricting the evaluation point
to the divertor target. Its locus and charge-state aggregation follow the
corresponding
[neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target),
while the species is krypton rather than neon.

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Number density of the lithium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for ionized lithium at the sheath entrance, summed
over positive ionization states and excluding neutral lithium.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the lithium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for ionized lithium at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the
lithium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local lithium-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the number of ionized lithium ions in the local
plasma volume $V$, with the count summed over all positive lithium
ionization states.

This quantity applies to the ionized lithium population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and uses a charge-state-summed aggregation. Neutral
lithium atoms, electrons, and ions of other elements are excluded.

Unlike [lithium_density_at_limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter), which
is evaluated at a limiter, this quantity is evaluated at the divertor-target
sheath entrance. It therefore represents the divertor-target member of the
lithium-density family rather than a limiter or general plasma-boundary
value.

NAMES.name: maximum_of_energy_flux_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Maximum local energy-deposition rate per unit area on a divertor target,
representing the peak combined load from incident plasma and radiative
energy carriers.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the peak local energy flux deposited on the plasma-facing
surface of one divertor target. It represents the highest surface energy
load, rather than the total energy deposited over the target.

The peak is defined by

$$
q_{E,\mathrm{peak}} = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in A_{\mathrm{target}}} q_E(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $q_{E,\mathrm{peak}}$ is the maximum energy flux, $q_E(\mathbf{x})$ is
the local energy flux at surface position $\mathbf{x}$, and
$A_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the plasma-facing surface of the divertor target.

The quantity combines all incident plasma-particle and radiative
energy-carrying channels included in
[energy_flux_at_divertor_target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target). The
maximum is taken over the specified target surface; inner and outer targets
are distinct target instances and are not summed under this name. It
excludes integration over target area, which instead defines the deposited
power represented by
[power_at_divertor_target](name:power_at_divertor_target), and it is not
restricted to the field-aligned component represented by parallel heat flux.

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Number density of neon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance, summed over Ne1+ through Ne10+ and
excluding neutral neon.
NAMES.long:
Number density of neon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the neon-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local neon-ion number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{q=1}^{10} \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neon-ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the number of neon ions in charge state $q+$
within the local plasma volume $V$, $V$ is the local plasma volume, and $q$
is the positive integer neon charge-state number. The upper limit 10 denotes
fully stripped neon.

This quantity applies to the free neon-ion population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target on the plasma side of the electrostatic sheath. It is
summed over all positive neon charge states from Ne1+ through Ne10+,
counting each ion once; neutral neon atoms are excluded. It is not the
density of all ion species or the free-electron population represented by
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target).

This member specializes
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) by selecting
neon ions while retaining the same target-sheath evaluation locus. It is the
species-specific counterpart of related quantities such as
[oxygen_density_at_divertor_target](name:oxygen_density_at_divertor_target).

sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of the nitrogen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for nitrogen ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the nitrogen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for nitrogen ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the
nitrogen-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local nitrogen-ion number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_N = \frac{dN_N}{dV}
$$

where $N_N$ is the number of nitrogen ions in a small plasma volume $V$
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the nitrogen-ion population immediately adjacent to
the divertor target and is summed over all positive nitrogen ionization
states. The aggregation counts each nitrogen ion once, regardless of its
charge state.

Neutral nitrogen atoms are excluded, as are nitrogen-bearing particles that
are not represented as nitrogen ions. This quantity is distinct from
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target),
which counts free electrons, and from
[neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target),
which applies the same target-local density definition to neon ions.

As a species-specific component, this quantity is one member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target); the parent
represents the same target-local number-density concept for a specified
species or species group.

sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Number density of the oxygen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for oxygen ions at the sheath entrance, summed
over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral oxygen.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the oxygen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the oxygen-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local oxygen-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\rm O} = \frac{dN_{\rm O}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\rm O}$ is the total number of oxygen ions in a small plasma
volume $V$ centered at the sheath entrance on the plasma side of the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the oxygen-ion population at the specified divertor
target and sums the number densities of all positive oxygen ionization
states, counting each ion once. Neutral oxygen atoms are excluded;
therefore, it is distinct from [oxygen_density](name:oxygen_density), which
includes neutral oxygen as well as charged oxygen states.

The target-specific quantity has the same charge-state-summed convention as
[neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target),
while
[oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary)
represents the corresponding oxygen-ion density at the plasma boundary
without this divertor-target locus.
