NAMES.name: temperature_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short:
Temperature at the divertor target is the energy-equivalent temperature of a
specified plasma population evaluated at the plasma side of a
divertor-target sheath. It refers to the sheath-entrance plasma population,
not to the solid target material or to an average over different
populations.
NAMES.long:
Temperature at the divertor target is the energy-equivalent temperature of a
specified plasma population evaluated at the plasma side of a
divertor-target sheath. It characterizes the random kinetic part of the
particle distribution at the sheath entrance, the boundary at which
sheath-entry conditions such as the Bohm criterion are posed, and is not a
thermodynamic property of the solid target material.

For a population $s$, the scalar target temperature is the one-third trace
of the kinetic thermal-energy moment over the velocity-space domain of that
population at the sheath entrance:

$$
T_{s,t} = \frac{m_s}{3 n_{s,t}} \int_{\mathcal{V}_{s,t}} |\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_{s,t}|^2 f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $T_{s,t}$ is the temperature at the divertor target for population
$s$, subscript $t$ denotes the divertor-target sheath entrance, $m_s$ is the
particle mass of population $s$, $n_{s,t}$ is the number density of that
population at the sheath entrance, $\mathcal{V}_{s,t}$ is the full
velocity-space domain of the specified sheath-entrance population,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,t}$ is the mean flow
velocity of the population at the sheath entrance, $f_{s,t}$ is its velocity
distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The
distribution normalization is such that integrating $f_{s,t}$ over
$\mathcal{V}_{s,t}$ gives $n_{s,t}$.

The specified population can be an electron population, an ion population, a
charge state, or another plasma population identified separately. If a
species is represented without charge-state resolution, this intensive value
is the density-weighted mean over all charge states. The unqualified
quantity does not imply an average over different plasma populations or over
positions on the divertor target.

For the electron population it corresponds to the [electron temperature at
divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target), and for the
ion population it corresponds to the [ion temperature at divertor
target](name:ion_temperature_at_divertor_target). It is the divertor-target
specialization of the more general [plasma
temperature](name:plasma_temperature). The moment definition makes it two
thirds of the population-averaged random kinetic energy at the sheath
entrance, not the full mean random kinetic energy per particle.

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per
particle of the electron population evaluated at the plasma side of a
divertor-target sheath, distinct from the target material temperature.
NAMES.long:
Electron temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per
particle of the electron population evaluated at the plasma side of a
divertor-target sheath. It is a plasma boundary quantity for electrons at
the downstream end of the scrape-off layer, not a thermodynamic property of
the solid target material.

For the electron population, the target temperature is the one-third trace
of the kinetic thermal-energy moment at the sheath edge:

$$
T_{e,t} = \frac{m_e}{3 n_{e,t}} \int |\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_{e,t}|^2 f_{e,t}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $T_{e,t}$ is the electron temperature at the divertor target, $m_e$ is
the electron mass, $n_{e,t}$ is the free-electron number density at the
sheath edge, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{e,t}$ is the
mean electron flow velocity at the sheath edge, $f_{e,t}(\mathbf{v})$ is the
electron velocity distribution there, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space
volume element.

This quantity applies exclusively to the free-electron population at a
specified divertor target and represents a density-weighted per-particle
thermal energy scale rather than an extensive sum. It excludes ion,
neutral-particle, and solid-target temperatures, and it is not an average
over multiple plasma populations.

It is the electron-specific component of [temperature at the divertor
target](name:temperature_at_divertor_target). The electron density at the
same locus, [electron density at divertor
target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), supplies the local
population density appearing in the defining moment but is a distinct
quantity.

NAMES.name: ion_temperature_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Ion temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per particle of
the ion population averaged over ion species and evaluated at the plasma
side of a divertor-target sheath, distinct from the target material
temperature.
NAMES.long:
Ion temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per particle of
the ion population averaged over ion species and evaluated at the plasma
side of a divertor-target sheath. It is a plasma boundary quantity for ions
at the downstream end of the scrape-off layer, not a thermodynamic property
of the solid target material.

For the ion population, the species-averaged target temperature is defined
from the ion kinetic thermal-energy moments by:

$$
T_{i,t} = \left\langle \frac{m_s}{3 n_{s,t}} \int \lvert \mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_{s,t} \rvert^2 f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_s
$$

where $T_{i,t}$ is the ion temperature at the divertor target, $i$
identifies the ion population, $t$ identifies the divertor-target
sheath-edge locus, $s$ indexes the included ion species, $m_s$ is the mass
of species $s$, $n_{s,t}$ is its number density at the target sheath edge,
$\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,t}$ is the mean flow velocity
of species $s$ there, $f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})$ is its velocity distribution,
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and angle brackets denote
averaging over the included ion species.

This quantity applies exclusively to the ion population immediately upstream
of a specified divertor target and represents an intensive, per-particle
thermal-energy scale averaged over ion species. It is not an extensive sum
of ion energies or densities, and it excludes electron, neutral-particle,
and solid-target temperatures.

It is the ion-specific component of [temperature at the divertor
target](name:temperature_at_divertor_target). Unlike [electron temperature
at the divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target), it
describes ion kinetic thermal energy at the same plasma-side target locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion temperature (average over ion species)

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Number density of the tritium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for tritium ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the tritium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the tritium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local tritium ion number density is defined by the positive-ion count:

$$
n_T = n_{T^+} = \frac{dN_T}{dV}
$$

where $n_T$ is the tritium ion number density, $n_{T^+}$ is the number
density of singly ionized tritium ions, $N_T$ is the number of tritium ions
in a small plasma volume, and $V$ is that plasma volume as its center
approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to the tritium ion population immediately adjacent to
the divertor target and is summed over all positive atomic ionization
states; for tritium, the included atomic ion is $T^+$. Neutral tritium atoms
and molecules, electrons, deuterium ions, and other ion species are
excluded.

It specializes [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target)
by selecting only tritium ions. Unlike
[deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target),
it does not aggregate the deuterium and tritium fuel-ion populations.

sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Number density of tungsten ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary, summed over positive ionization states and
excluding neutral tungsten.
NAMES.long:
Number density of tungsten ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the tungsten-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The charge-state-summed tungsten number density is defined by

$$
n_W = \sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{W^{Z+}}
$$

where $n_W$ is the total local number density of tungsten ions, $n_{W^{Z+}}$
is the local number density of tungsten ions with positive charge state $Z$,
and $Z$ is the integer tungsten ionization state from 1 through 74.

This quantity applies only to tungsten ions immediately upstream of the
electrostatic sheath at a divertor target. It includes every positive
tungsten ionization state once, without charge-state weighting, and excludes
neutral tungsten atoms and ions of all other elements.

The charge-state sum makes this the species-level tungsten component of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target). Its
divertor-target locus distinguishes it from
[tungsten_density_at_limiter](name:tungsten_density_at_limiter), which
describes tungsten ion density at a limiter, and from
[tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which applies at the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Number density of the xenon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for xenon ions at the sheath entrance immediately
upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the xenon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for xenon ions at the sheath entrance immediately
upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the xenon-specific
member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local xenon ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{Xe}}$
is the number of included xenon ions, and $V$ is a local plasma volume whose
center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to the xenon-ion population immediately adjacent to
one divertor target and is summed over all positive xenon ionization states,
from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon. Neutral xenon atoms are
excluded; this is a local sheath-entrance density, not a volume-averaged
density or a density at a general plasma location.

Compared with [xenon_density](name:xenon_density), which denotes xenon ion
density at a general plasma point, this quantity is specialized to the
divertor-target sheath entrance. Its charge-state-summed species convention
parallels
[oxygen_density_at_divertor_target](name:oxygen_density_at_divertor_target),
with xenon replacing oxygen.

NAMES.name: density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of a selected plasma population evaluated at the
plasma boundary, the last closed magnetic flux surface separating confined
plasma from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density at the plasma boundary is the amount of a selected
particle population per physical volume at the boundary of magnetically
confined plasma. The population is intentionally unspecified by this parent
quantity and is fixed by each specialized instance.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_P(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\int f_P(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_P$ is the number density of population $P$, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a
point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_P$ is the velocity distribution function of population $P$, and
$d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called
the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. The selected population may be an electron population, an
ion or impurity population, a neutral population, an elemental population,
or an effective isotope mixture. The aggregation convention is additive over
exactly the particles included in population $P$; inclusion of neutral
particles and summation over charge states are specialization-dependent and
are not fixed by this subject-less parent quantity. This boundary quantity
is distinct from [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis)
and [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter), which use different loci.

Specialized instances fix the population and its aggregation convention:
[electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary)
selects electrons, while
[krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary)
selects krypton ions with charge-state aggregation. Elemental variants such
as [boron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary)
may include both neutral atoms and ionic charge states. When population and
aggregation are held fixed, the corresponding boundary value is the
locus-specific counterpart of density evaluated at another defined plasma
location.

NAMES.name: beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short:
Number density of beryllium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally
on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization
states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of beryllium ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the beryllium-ion
population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma
boundary is the separatrix separating magnetically confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining density is the zeroth velocity-space moment, summed over all
beryllium ionization states:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Be}}}\int f_{\mathrm{Be},z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$
is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $z$ identifies a beryllium
ionization state, $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the set of included
beryllium ionization states, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$f_{\mathrm{Be},z}$ is the velocity distribution function for state $z$, and
$d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity applies locally at the plasma boundary and is additive over all
included ionic charge states. It includes beryllium ions and excludes
neutral beryllium atoms; it is not a flux-surface average.

This is the beryllium-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), whose
particle population is unspecified. It differs from
[flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary)
because that quantity averages the beryllium-ion density over the boundary
surface, and from
[beryllium_density_at_limiter](name:beryllium_density_at_limiter), which
uses a limiter-adjacent locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: boron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short:
Number density of boron at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic
flux surface, summed over neutral atoms and all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of boron at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive
particle count per physical volume for elemental boron evaluated on the last
closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed
magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off-layer region.

The local elemental-boron number density at a boundary point is the zeroth
velocity moment summed over neutral boron and all ionic charge states:

$$
n_{\mathrm B}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{z=0}^{5} \int f_{\mathrm B,z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm B}$ is the elemental-boron number density, $\mathrm B$
denotes boron, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux
surface, $t$ is time, $z$ is the boron charge-state index with $z=0$
denoting neutral boron and $z=1$ through $5$ denoting the ionic states,
$f_{\mathrm B,z}$ is the phase-space distribution function for that state,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element.

This quantity applies specifically to elemental boron and includes neutral
atoms together with all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+. It
is a local value at the plasma boundary, with no averaging over the boundary
surface or over a volume, and excludes densities of other elements and
electrons. Unlike
[ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), it is
not restricted to charged ions.

It is the boron-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
[flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary)
applies the same neutral-plus-ionic boron aggregation but averages the
density over the last closed magnetic flux surface rather than giving the
local boundary value.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Boron (B)

NAMES.name: carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short:
Number density of carbon impurity ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated
locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all
ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of carbon ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the carbon-ion population evaluated on the
last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix
separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment, with explicit aggregation over
carbon ionization states, is

$$
n_C(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{q=1}^{6}\int f_{C^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_C$ is the carbon-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on
the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $q$ is the integer carbon charge-state
index, $f_{C^{q+}}$ is the velocity distribution function of carbon ions in
charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is
the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies locally to carbon ions in charge states C+ through C6+
and is summed over those ionization states. Neutral carbon is excluded, and
the value is not averaged over the boundary flux surface.

It specializes the population-unspecified
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) to carbon
ions. It is distinct from
[flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which applies the same carbon-ion aggregation after averaging over the
boundary surface, and from [carbon_density](name:carbon_density), whose
elemental scope includes neutral carbon as well as ionic charge states.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short:
Number density of deuterium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally
on the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over all ionic charge
states, and excluding neutral deuterium.
NAMES.long:
Number density of deuterium ions at the plasma boundary is the local
particle count per physical volume for the deuterium-ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the separatrix separating magnetically confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_D(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{z>0}\int f_{D^{z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_D$ is the deuterium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point
on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $z$ is a positive ionic charge state,
$D^{z+}$ denotes deuterium in charge state $z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_{D^{z+}}$ is the velocity distribution function for that charge
state, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to deuterium ions, is evaluated locally
at the plasma boundary, and is additive over all included positive deuterium
charge states. Neutral deuterium atoms and molecules are excluded. It is
therefore distinct from the broader
[ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), which
does not select deuterium, and from
[flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which applies a flux-surface average rather than a local boundary
evaluation.

This species-specific quantity is a specialization of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), whose
particle population and charge-state aggregation are unspecified. The local
deuterium value provides the pointwise boundary quantity from which the
corresponding flux-surface-averaged deuterium density is formed.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short:
Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species at the
plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per
physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species at the
plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume
for that effective species evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux
surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface
separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local effective deuterium-tritium number density is the zeroth velocity
moment of its distribution function at a boundary point:

$$
n_{DT}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_{DT}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{DT}$ is the effective deuterium-tritium fuel-pseudo-species number
density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface,
$t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity of the effective pseudo-species,
$f_{DT}$ is its phase-space distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies to the deuterium-tritium fuel mixture represented as
one effective pseudo-species, rather than to separate deuterium and tritium
populations. It is a local boundary value with no averaging over the
boundary surface or over a volume, and no additional charge-state
aggregation is implied by the effective-species representation.

It is the deuterium-tritium-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). Unlike
[flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary),
it denotes the local value at the plasma boundary rather than an average
over that last closed magnetic flux surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of electrons at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic
flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of electrons at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive
particle count per physical volume for the electron population evaluated on
the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting
closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local electron number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the
electron distribution function at a boundary point:

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_e(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the
last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron
velocity, $f_e$ is the electron phase-space distribution function, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to electrons and is not an ion or
neutral-particle density. It is a local boundary value, with no averaging
over the boundary surface or over a volume; because electrons are not
resolved here into atomic ionization states, no charge-state aggregation is
applied.

It is the electron-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
[flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary)
instead represents the average of electron density over the same last closed
magnetic flux surface, rather than the local value.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron number density averaged over the entire last closed magnetic flux
surface, giving the separatrix value across the confined-plasma and
scrape-off-layer interface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged electron number density on the
separatrix, the last closed magnetic flux surface forming the
confined-plasma boundary. It represents the electron population at the
complete core–scrape-off-layer interface after averaging over the boundary
surface.

For a magnetic-flux surface labeled by $\psi$, the separatrix value is
defined by

$$
\langle n_e\rangle_{\rm sep} =
\frac{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\rm sep}} n_e\,\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\rm sep}}\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

where $\langle n_e\rangle_{\rm sep}$ is the flux-surface-averaged electron
number density at the separatrix, $n_e$ is the local electron number
density, $S_{\rm sep}$ is the separatrix surface, $dS$ is its differential
surface element, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux surface label, and $\nabla\psi$
is the spatial gradient of that label.

The average covers the entire last closed flux surface at the
core–scrape-off-layer boundary. It is an electron-specific quantity, with no
ion or neutral population included and no ionization-state summation. It is
distinct from the local, pointwise boundary value
[electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which is not flux-surface averaged.

The analogous
[flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary)
applies the same separatrix averaging convention to the ion population
rather than the electron population.

sources.parent_definition: Electron density

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the
local particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux
surface and summed over charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the helium-3 ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the limiting closed magnetic flux surface, or separatrix, separating
confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local charge-state-summed helium-3 number density is the zeroth velocity
moment of the helium-3 ion distribution functions at a boundary point:

$$
n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q=1}^{2} \int f_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},q}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density,
$\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is
time, $q$ is the helium-3 ionic charge state, $f_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},q}$ is
the phase-space distribution function for that charge state, $\mathbf{v}$ is
ion velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to helium-3 ions, whose nuclei contain
three nucleons, and includes all ionized charge states from singly charged
through fully stripped helium-3. It excludes neutral helium-3, other helium
isotopes, and other plasma species. The value is local at the boundary and
is not averaged over the boundary surface or over a volume.

It is the helium-3-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
[flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary)
represents the average of this local helium-3 ion density over the same last
closed magnetic flux surface rather than its value at a boundary point.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He)

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on
the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the helium-4 ion population evaluated on the
last closed magnetic flux surface. It represents the charge-state-summed
helium-4 ion population at that locus.

The defining charge-state-summed zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_q\int f_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},q}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density,
$\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $q$ is the
ionic charge-state index, $f_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},q}$ is the velocity
distribution function of helium-4 ions in charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called
the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. This quantity applies only to helium-4 ions, is evaluated
locally at the boundary, includes all helium-4 ionic charge states, and
excludes neutral helium-4 atoms.

As a species-specific instance of [particle number density at the plasma
boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), it fixes the otherwise
unspecified population to helium-4 ions. It differs from
[flux-surface-averaged helium-4 density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which averages the same charge-state-summed population over the boundary
surface, and from [helium-3 density at the plasma
boundary](name:helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary), which selects a
different helium isotope.

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on
the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all hydrogen ion
charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the hydrogen-ion population on the last closed
magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_H(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\int f_H(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_H$ is the hydrogen-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on
the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_H$
is the hydrogen-ion velocity distribution function, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is
the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity is evaluated locally at the plasma boundary and is summed over
the included hydrogen ion charge states. It excludes neutral hydrogen and is
distinct from electron density and from the total ion population represented
by [ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The corresponding surface-averaged quantity,
[flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary),
applies the same hydrogen-ion population to an average over the boundary
surface rather than a local evaluation. The subject-unspecified parent
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) defines the
common boundary-density concept, while this quantity fixes the population as
hydrogen ions.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen (H)

NAMES.name: ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Number density of ions at the plasma boundary, encompassing
species-selective and total charged-ion populations with local or
flux-surface-averaged evaluation on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of ions at the plasma boundary is the particle count per
physical volume for an ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic
flux surface, with the representation either local or averaged over that
surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface
separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local ion number density at a boundary point is the zeroth velocity
moment of the ion distribution function:

$$
n_i(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_i(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_i$ is the local ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on
the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion
velocity, $f_i$ is the phase-space distribution function of the selected ion
population, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies to charged ions and may describe a selected ion
population or an aggregate over charged ion species and charge states. Its
spatial representation may be a local boundary value or an average over the
last closed magnetic flux surface. Neutral particles and electrons are
excluded; consequently, it is distinct from [electron density at the plasma
boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary) and from
neutral-particle density.

This is the ion-specific branch of [density at the plasma
boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). [Flux-surface-averaged ion
density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) applies
the same ion-density concept after averaging over the boundary surface,
while [total ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) applies the aggregation
over all charged ion species and charge states while excluding neutrals.

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Number density of iron impurity ions at the plasma boundary, the last closed
flux surface separating the magnetically confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off layer, summed over all ion charge states from Fe+
through fully stripped Fe26+.
NAMES.long:
Iron density at the plasma boundary is the number of iron impurity ions per
unit volume — summed over all ion charge states from singly ionized Fe$^+$
through fully stripped Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic number $Z = 26$) — evaluated at
the separatrix, the last closed flux surface separating the magnetically
confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It represents the
charge-state-summed iron impurity concentration on that boundary.

The charge-state aggregation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron ion number density at the plasma
boundary, $z$ is the positive ion charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$
is the partial number density of iron ions in charge state $z+$ at the same
boundary; these number-density variables have the unit specified for this
standard name.

The sum is over ion charge states only, so neutral iron Fe$^0$ is excluded.
As a scalar number density, the quantity is non-negative, with zero denoting
absence of iron ions at the plasma boundary. It is distinct from
[flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which denotes a flux-surface-averaged boundary value rather than the local
boundary density.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Number density of lithium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on
the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of lithium ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the lithium-ion population evaluated on the
last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix
separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining charge-state-summed zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{Z=1}^{3}\int f_{\mathrm{Li}^{Z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is
a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $Z$ is the lithium
ionization-state index, $f_{\mathrm{Li}^{Z+}}$ is the velocity distribution
function for lithium ions in charge state $Z+$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity is local at the plasma boundary and is not averaged over the
boundary flux surface. It includes lithium ions from Li+ through Li3+,
summed over these charge states, and excludes neutral lithium. It is the
lithium-specific specialization of [density at the plasma
boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary).

The corresponding flux-surface-averaged quantity, [flux-surface-averaged
lithium density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary),
applies a flux-surface average to the same charge-state-summed lithium-ion
density. The boundary locus also distinguishes this quantity from [lithium
density at the limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter), which is evaluated
at a limiter rather than at the plasma boundary.

sources.parent_definition: Lithium (Li)

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Number density of neon ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the
last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
Number density of neon ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the neon-ion population evaluated on the last
closed magnetic flux surface. The population is summed over all ionization
stages from singly ionized neon, Ne$^+$, through fully stripped neon,
Ne$^{10+}$.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x}_b)=\int f_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neon-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a
point on the plasma boundary, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity,
$f_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the velocity distribution function aggregated over the
included neon ion charge states, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space
volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called
the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. This quantity is evaluated locally at that boundary and is
not averaged over the flux surface. It includes neon ions across all charge
states from Ne$^+$ through Ne$^{10+}$ and excludes neutral neon and other
particle species.

This quantity is the neon-specific specialization of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). It is
distinct from
[flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which applies the same charge-state aggregation to a flux-surface average
rather than a local boundary value.

sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Number density of nitrogen ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the
local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed
magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of nitrogen ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the nitrogen ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from
the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local nitrogen ion number density at a boundary point is the zeroth
velocity moment summed over ionic charge states:

$$
n_N(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q=1}^{7} \int f_{N^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_N$ is the nitrogen ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on
the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $q$ is the positive
integer ionic charge state, $N^{q+}$ is a nitrogen ion with charge state
$q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, $f_{N^{q+}}$ is the phase-space
distribution function for that charge state, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to nitrogen ions and is summed over
charge states from singly ionized nitrogen through fully stripped nitrogen.
It excludes neutral nitrogen and electron density, and it is a local
boundary value with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume.

It is the nitrogen-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
[flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary)
instead averages the same charge-state-summed nitrogen ion density over the
last closed magnetic flux surface.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen (N)

NAMES.name: total_power_at_separatrix
NAMES.short:
Net energy power leaving the confined plasma through the last closed
magnetic flux surface and entering the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Separatrix power is the net global energy loss from the confined plasma into
the scrape-off layer across the last closed magnetic flux surface. It
represents the aggregate power crossing the entire separatrix rather than a
local surface value.

The defining boundary integral is

$$
P_{\rm sep} = \oint_{S_{\rm sep}} \mathbf{S}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\rm sep}$ is the separatrix power, $S_{\rm sep}$ is the last
closed magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{S}_E$ is the net plasma-energy flux
density, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the confined
plasma toward the scrape-off layer, and $dA$ is an element of separatrix
area.

This is a total, net quantity integrated over the complete separatrix. It
applies to the confined plasma as a whole, with no selection of species,
reaction channel, or individual transport mechanism; outward energy transfer
is the plasma loss represented by the quantity. It is not a pointwise
energy-flux density or a power associated with a single surface location.

The boundary total is distinct from [radiated power over the core
region](name:radiated_power_over_core_region), which describes
electromagnetic power emitted within the core and is not necessarily equal
to power crossing the separatrix. It is also distinct from [power due to
conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction), which describes
conduction-mediated power deposited on plasma-facing surfaces downstream of
the separatrix.

sources.parent_definition: Power through separatrix

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Number density of tritium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the
local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed
magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of tritium ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the tritium-ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from
the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local tritium-ion number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the
tritium-ion distribution function at a boundary point:

$$
n_\mathrm{T}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_\mathrm{T}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_\mathrm{T}$ is the tritium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a
point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is
tritium-ion velocity, $f_\mathrm{T}$ is the tritium-ion phase-space
distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to ionized tritium and excludes neutral
tritium, deuterium, protium, electrons, impurity ions, and total ion
density. It is a local boundary value, with no averaging over the boundary
surface or over a volume; for tritium, the relevant positive ion population
is singly ionized tritium, so no aggregation over multiple positive
ionization stages is applied.

It is the tritium-specific instance of [density at the plasma
boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
[flux-surface-averaged tritium density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary)
instead represents the average of tritium-ion density over the same last
closed magnetic flux surface, while [hydrogen density at the plasma
boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [deuterium density
at the plasma boundary](name:deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary) refer to
different hydrogen-isotope ion populations.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Number density of xenon ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on
the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
Number density of xenon ions at the plasma boundary is the amount of the
xenon ion population per physical volume at the last closed magnetic flux
surface. It is the local boundary value, not a flux-surface average.

The local charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{Z=1}^{54}\int f_{\mathrm{Xe},Z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a
point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $Z$ is the xenon ion charge-state
number, $f_{\mathrm{Xe},Z}$ is the velocity distribution function for charge
state $Z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the
velocity-space volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called
the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. The aggregation is additive over all xenon ion charge
states from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral
xenon atoms. The value is local at the boundary rather than averaged over
that surface.

This entry specializes the population-unspecified
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) to xenon ions.
The corresponding
[flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary)
applies the same xenon charge-state aggregation after averaging over the
plasma-boundary flux surface, so it is distinct from this local quantity.

NAMES.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless radial magnetic-surface label locating the H-mode edge
transport-barrier pedestal between the magnetic axis and the last closed
flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the dimensionless radial magnetic-surface coordinate
assigned to the pedestal position of an H-mode edge transport barrier. It
identifies the flux surface associated with that position, rather than a
density, pressure, or temperature value evaluated there.

The normalized poloidal-flux coordinate is defined from the poloidal
magnetic flux by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{p}} = \left(\frac{\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}\right)^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the normalized poloidal-flux coordinate, $\psi$
is poloidal magnetic flux, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is its value on the
magnetic axis, and $\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}}$ is its value on the last
closed magnetic flux surface. The reported value is this coordinate
evaluated at the pedestal position.

This quantity applies specifically to the H-mode edge transport-barrier
pedestal locus. It has no species, population, or field-component dependence
and involves no averaging or summation over plasma quantities. It retains
the generic pedestal-position meaning and is not a pedestal-top profile
value or a maximum-gradient location.

It is a locus-specific instance of the parent [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate), applying that
coordinate's outward magnetic-surface labeling to the pedestal position
rather than to an arbitrary nested surface. For a pedestal within nested
closed surfaces, its value lies between zero at the magnetic axis and one at
the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: safety_factor_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short:
Signed field-line winding ratio on the flux surface at the core-side
shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, counting toroidal turns per
poloidal circuit.
NAMES.long:
The pedestal-top safety factor is the signed field-line winding ratio on the
flux surface at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
It is a local flux-surface value rather than a gradient or an average over
the pedestal region.

The value is inherited from the flux-increment definition of the [safety
factor](name:safety_factor) and evaluated on the pedestal-top flux surface:

$$
q_{\rm ped} = \left. \frac{d\Phi_{\rm tor}}{d(\Phi_{\rm pol}/2\pi)} \right|_{\rm ped}
$$

where $q_{\rm ped}$ is the pedestal-top safety factor, $\Phi_{\rm tor}$ is
the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the flux surface, $\Phi_{\rm pol}$ is
the poloidal magnetic flux associated with the flux-surface boundary, and
the subscript $\rm ped$ denotes evaluation at the pedestal top.

This quantity applies to the single flux surface at the core-side shoulder
of the H-mode edge transport barrier and has no species, mode, or interval
aggregation. It is distinct from
[safety_factor_at_normalized_poloidal_magnetic_flux_equal_to_0_95](name:safety_factor_at_normalized_poloidal_magnetic_flux_equal_to_0_95),
which is evaluated at a fixed normalized poloidal-flux label rather than at
the pedestal-defined locus. The
[safety_factor_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:safety_factor_at_internal_transport_barrier)
is a corresponding locus-specific value at a different transport barrier.

The orientation is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the toroidal magnetic field and plasma
current are parallel, directed in the same sense along increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$; negative when they are antiparallel.

NAMES.name: thermal_plasma_pressure
NAMES.short:
Thermal plasma pressure is the equilibrium isotropic kinetic pressure of
thermal electrons and ions, summed over represented ion species and
excluding fast-particle contributions.
NAMES.long:
Thermal plasma pressure is the isotropic kinetic pressure of thermal
electron and ion populations in a fluid or magnetohydrodynamic description.
It represents equilibrium mechanical stress from these populations and is
not a perturbation amplitude.

For the included thermal populations, the pressure is defined by

$$
p_{\rm th} = p_{e,\rm th} + \sum_{s \in \mathcal{I}} p_{s,\rm th}
$$

where $p_{\rm th}$ is the thermal plasma pressure, $p_{e,\rm th}$ is the
thermal electron pressure, $p_{s,\rm th}$ is the thermal pressure of ion
species $s$, and $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of represented ion species.

The quantity applies to the thermal electron population and all represented
thermal ion species, with ion contributions aggregated over the included
species and charge states. It excludes fast-particle and other nonthermal
contributions, neutral-particle pressure, magnetic pressure, dynamic ram
pressure, anisotropic pressure components, and first-order pressure
perturbations.

Thermal plasma pressure is the thermal specialization of [plasma
pressure](name:plasma_pressure), obtained by restricting the parent quantity
to thermal electrons and ions. [Thermal ion
pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure) supplies the ion contribution in the
defining sum, while the electron contribution is included separately.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short:
Non-negative radius-like toroidal-flux label identifying the magnetic flux
surface at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the non-negative, radius-like toroidal-flux label of the
magnetic flux surface at the H-mode [pedestal
top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal), the core-side
shoulder of the edge transport barrier. It locates that surface on the
physical toroidal-flux scale rather than specifying a geometric distance.

The coordinate is defined from enclosed toroidal magnetic flux by:

$$
\rho_{\rm tor} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\rm tor}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\rho_{\rm tor}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate, $\Phi_{\rm tor}$ is
the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux, $B_0$ is the positive reference vacuum
toroidal-field magnitude that sets the coordinate scale, and $\pi$ is the
circular constant.

The value applies to the single nested magnetic flux surface passing through
the pedestal top. It is a local flux-surface label, not a flux-surface or
volume average, and it has no particle-population or charge-state
aggregation.

This is the pedestal-top specialization of the parent [toroidal flux
coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate), obtained by evaluating that
coordinate on the pedestal-top surface. Unlike the [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate at the pedestal
top](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top), it retains
the radius-like physical scale of the toroidal flux coordinate.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_neutral_temperature
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged neutral temperature is the translational kinetic
temperature, expressed as energy per particle, of a neutral population
throughout the plasma volume inside the last closed magnetic flux surface
during plasma initiation.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged neutral temperature is the translational kinetic temperature
of a neutral population during plasma initiation, representing random
translational energy after removal of mean flow. It excludes energy stored
in internal excitation or other internal quantum states.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_{n} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}\int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} T_n(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\overline{T}_{n}$ is the volume-averaged neutral temperature,
$T_n(\mathbf{x})$ is the local translational kinetic temperature of the
neutral population at position $\mathbf{x}$, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the
plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and
$\mathrm{d}V$ is the differential physical-volume element.

The quantity applies to the represented neutral population throughout the
volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface during plasma
initiation. Its aggregation convention is an arithmetic spatial volume
average of the local temperature, not a local value or a density-weighted
particle average. It does not select only the cold or energetic neutral
component and is not restricted to a particular internal quantum state.

This quantity is obtained by applying the volume-averaging transformation to
[neutral temperature](name:neutral_temperature), with the local population
and state aggregation inherited from that quantity. [Cold neutral
temperature](name:cold_neutral_temperature) and [hot neutral
temperature](name:hot_neutral_temperature) are population-restricted
alternatives, while [neutral internal state
temperature](name:neutral_internal_state_temperature) resolves a specified
internal state rather than the generic neutral population.

NAMES.name: frequency_of_wave_diagnostic_channel
NAMES.short:
Temporal frequency associated with a wave-diagnostic channel, defining the
oscillation or probing frequency used to establish its plasma interaction.
NAMES.long:
The wave-diagnostic-channel frequency is the temporal rate of oscillation of
the electromagnetic wave associated with a channel. It specifies the
frequency at which the channel interacts with or samples the plasma.

The relation between temporal frequency $f$ and angular frequency $\omega$
is

$$
f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}
$$

where $f$ is the temporal frequency, $\omega$ is the angular frequency of
the wave, and $\pi$ is the mathematical circle constant.

This quantity applies to one wave-diagnostic channel and is not a sum or
average over channels, frequency values, or wave power. For a
frequency-swept probing channel, each selected frequency defines the probing
state used to determine the corresponding plasma response or cutoff
location; for a resonance channel, it identifies the wave frequency
associated with the probed resonance.

The channel-owned quantity is distinct from the broader [wave
frequency](name:wave_frequency) concept and from the beam-owned [frequency
of an electron-cyclotron beam](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_beam).
It describes frequency, not the duration of a sweep or the electromagnetic
energy-transfer rate represented by [wave power](name:wave_power).

NAMES.name: length_of_interferometer_beam
NAMES.short:
Effective optical path length accumulated by an interferometer beam along
its propagation path, providing the reference for signed plasma-induced
path-length variations.
NAMES.long:
The interferometer-beam length is the effective optical path accumulated by
the electromagnetic wave along its propagation path. It is a path-integrated
length, not a local geometric coordinate or a plasma-induced difference.

For a beam path $\Gamma$, the effective optical path length is defined as

$$
L = \int_{\Gamma} n(s)\,ds
$$

where $L$ is the effective optical path length, $\Gamma$ is the complete
interferometer-beam propagation path, $s$ is geometric arclength along that
path, and $n(s)$ is the local phase refractive index encountered by the
wave.

The quantity applies to the complete designated beam path and aggregates the
local optical contributions by path integration. It represents the path
length itself, rather than a signed change from a reference state; it is not
restricted to a particular plasma population or region.

The related [variation of length of an interferometer
beam](name:variation_of_length_of_interferometer_beam) is the signed
difference between the plasma-present path length $L_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ and
the corresponding no-plasma reference length $L_{\mathrm{reference}}$,
expressed inline as $\Delta L = L_{\mathrm{plasma}} -
L_{\mathrm{reference}}$, where $\Delta L$ is the path-length variation,
$L_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the effective path length with plasma present, and
$L_{\mathrm{reference}}$ is the effective path length for the same beam path
without plasma.

NAMES.name: line_integrated_electron_number_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Free-electron column density accumulated along a complete electromagnetic
propagation path, including both forward and return segments when present.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the column density of free electrons encountered along a
specified electromagnetic propagation path. It represents the total
free-electron content accumulated along the path, rather than the local
electron population at a point.

For the complete propagation path, the line-integrated electron density is
defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{line}} = \int_{\Gamma_{\mathrm{full}}} n_e(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the line-integrated electron density,
$n_e(\ell)$ is the local free-electron number density at path position
$\ell$, $\ell$ is arclength along the path, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{full}}$ is
the complete propagation path.

The integral applies to the free-electron population along the full line of
sight and aggregates the local number density over arclength. For a
reflected propagation channel, the path includes both forward and return
segments, with no factor-of-two correction. The quantity excludes neutral or
bound electrons and is distinct from the local [electron
density](name:electron_density) and from a path average.

For a path with total arclength $L$, this quantity relates to the
[line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density)
through $N_{e,\mathrm{line}} = L\bar{n}_e$, where $L$ is the total path
arclength and $\bar{n}_e$ is the path-averaged free-electron number density.

NAMES.name: polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam
NAMES.short:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the polarization ellipse of a
polarimeter beam after propagation through magnetized plasma. It describes
the beam's post-propagation transverse polarization state, not the incident
state or the ellipse orientation.
NAMES.long:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the polarization ellipse of a
polarimeter beam after propagation through magnetized plasma is the
ellipticity of that beam. It characterizes the relative electric-field
semiamplitudes of the post-propagation transverse polarization ellipse.

The ellipticity is defined by

$$
\varepsilon = \frac{b}{a}
$$

where $\varepsilon$ is the polarization ellipticity, $a$ is the major-axis
semiamplitude of the electric-field polarization ellipse, and $b$ is the
signed minor-axis semiamplitude of that ellipse. The magnitude satisfies
$|\varepsilon| \leq 1$.

This quantity applies to the polarimeter beam after it has traversed the
magnetized plasma and is therefore distinct from the [initial polarization
ellipticity](name:initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam). It
is a polarization-shape parameter and excludes the orientation of the
ellipse; rotation of that orientation is represented by the [Faraday
angle](name:faraday_angle). The quantity refers to a single beam
polarization state, with no aggregation over distinct beam paths.

Magnetized-plasma birefringence can transform the [initial polarization
ellipticity](name:initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam) into
this post-propagation ellipticity by changing the polarization ellipse
during propagation; that change is distinct from Faraday rotation of the
ellipse orientation.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the electric-field vector rotates in a
right-handed sense about the beam-propagation direction.

sources.leaf_definition: Ellipticity
sources.parent_definition: Set of channels (lines-of-sight)

NAMES.name: initial_polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam
NAMES.short:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the electric-field
polarization ellipse of a polarimeter probing beam in its incident state,
before plasma entry. It gives only the ellipticity component of the initial
polarization vector, not the ellipse orientation.
NAMES.long:
Signed ratio of the minor to major semiaxes of the electric-field
polarization ellipse of a polarimeter probing beam in its incident state,
before plasma entry, is the initial polarization ellipticity of that beam.
It is the ellipticity component of the beam's initial polarization vector
and specifies the shape and handedness of the incident polarization ellipse,
not its orientation.

For an incident electric-field polarization ellipse with major semiaxis
amplitude $a_0$ and minor semiaxis amplitude $b_0$, the initial ellipticity
$\epsilon_0$ is defined by:

$$
\epsilon_0 = \sigma_0 \frac{b_0}{a_0}
$$

where $\epsilon_0$ is the initial polarization ellipticity, $a_0$ is the
major semiaxis amplitude, $b_0$ is the minor semiaxis amplitude with $0 \le
b_0 \le a_0$, and $\sigma_0$ is the handedness sign of the incident
polarization state.

This quantity applies to a single polarimeter probing beam along a specified
line of sight in its pre-plasma state. It is not averaged or summed over
multiple lines of sight, and it does not describe the full polarization
vector, beam intensity, wavelength, path geometry, path-integrated
ellipticity, or any post-plasma polarization state.

It provides the reference value for Cotton-Mouton ellipticity changes
induced during traversal of magnetized plasma. It is the incident-state
counterpart of [polarization ellipticity of a polarimeter
beam](name:polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam), which denotes the
polarization ellipticity after plasma traversal; it is distinct from the
[Faraday angle](name:faraday_angle), which describes rotation of the
polarization-ellipse orientation rather than the semiaxis ratio.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when, in the right-handed beam-local basis
$(\hat{e}_1, \hat{e}_2, \hat{k})$ with $\hat{k}$ along beam propagation,
$\hat{e}_1$ along the major semiaxis, and $\hat{e}_2 = \hat{k} \times
\hat{e}_1$, the electric-field vector rotates from $+\hat{e}_1$ toward
$+\hat{e}_2$ as time increases.

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_measurement_position
NAMES.short:
Signed equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux function evaluated at a diagnostic
measurement location, identifying the nested magnetic surface intersecting
that location.
NAMES.long:
The signed poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$ is the equilibrium flux function
evaluated at a physical measurement position. It labels the nested magnetic
surface passing through that position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

For an axisymmetric equilibrium, the poloidal magnetic-flux function is
defined by

$$
\psi(R,Z) = \int_0^R B_Z(R',Z)\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $\psi(R,Z)$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at cylindrical coordinates
$(R,Z)$, $B_Z(R',Z)$ is the vertical magnetic-field component, $R$ and $R'$
are major-radius coordinates, $Z$ is vertical height, and $\pi$ is the
circle constant. The toroidal angle $\phi$ completes the right-handed
cylindrical frame; axisymmetry makes $\psi$ independent of $\phi$.

This quantity applies to the equilibrium magnetic field at one physical
measurement position and has no species or population restriction. It is a
point evaluation, not a sum, average, or integral over multiple measurement
positions. It is not a normalized flux coordinate and does not represent a
perturbation or fluctuation of the equilibrium flux.

The same flux-function definition is used for [poloidal magnetic flux at a
beam-tracing point](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_beam_tracing_point), but
that quantity differs in evaluation locus. A normalized surface label at the
same type of location is [normalized poloidal flux coordinate at a
measurement
position](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position),
which is derived by applying axis and boundary references to the signed flux
value.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the net vertical magnetic flux through the
defining horizontal disk is directed in the $+Z$ direction of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radiative_temperature_at_ece_channel
NAMES.short:
Equivalent blackbody temperature of electron cyclotron emission intensity
detected by a frequency-selective ECE channel, representing the radiation
brightness temperature.
NAMES.long:
Radiative temperature at an ECE channel is the equivalent blackbody
temperature associated with the detected electron cyclotron emission
intensity at that channel's selected frequency. It is a
brightness-temperature representation of the radiation, not the kinetic
temperature of the electron population.

For specific intensity represented by a blackbody spectrum, the radiation
temperature $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is defined by

$$
I_\nu = \frac{2h\nu^3}{c^2}\left[\exp\left(\frac{h\nu}{T_{\mathrm{rad}}}\right)-1\right]^{-1}
$$

where $I_\nu$ is the detected specific intensity at frequency $\nu$, $h$ is
Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light, and $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is the
energy-equivalent blackbody temperature.

The quantity applies to one ECE channel and its selected frequency; it is
not summed or averaged over channels. It excludes the separate kinetic
electron temperature and polarization-resolved radiation quantities. When
the emitting plasma is optically thick, $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ approaches the
local electron temperature. The [radiative temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:radiative_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) uses the same
brightness-temperature definition at a different evaluation locus.

NAMES.name: spectral_calibration_factor_at_line_of_sight
NAMES.short:
Wavelength-specific interferometric conversion coefficient that converts a
signed phase change along a line of sight into electron column density.
NAMES.long:
The spectral calibration factor is the wavelength-specific proportionality
that maps an interferometric phase change along one line of sight to the
electron column density on that optical path.

The conversion is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{line}} = K_{\mathrm{spec}}\,\Delta\varphi
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the [line-integrated electron number
density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density), $K_{\mathrm{spec}}$
is this spectral calibration factor, and $\Delta\varphi$ is the signed
interferometric phase change.

The factor applies to the complete electron-density integral along the
associated line of sight and to its corresponding probing wavelength. It
represents the electron contribution only and is not a local density, a
line-averaged density, or an optical phase itself.

Applying this factor produces the line-integrated electron number density;
dividing that result by the optical chord length gives [line-averaged
electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density). The associated
wavelength is the spectral parameter of the probing electromagnetic wave,
related to [wavelength of wave beam](name:wavelength_of_wave_beam).

NAMES.name: variation_of_length_of_interferometer_beam
NAMES.short:
Signed change in the effective optical path length accumulated along an
interferometer beam, caused by plasma relative to the corresponding
no-plasma reference path.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed plasma-induced change in effective optical path
length accumulated along one interferometer-beam line of sight. It captures
the integrated refractive effect of the plasma along that path rather than a
local geometric displacement.

The defining difference is

$$
\Delta L = L_{\mathrm{plasma}} - L_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\Delta L$ is the plasma-induced optical path-length variation,
$L_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the effective optical path length with the plasma
contribution present, and $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the corresponding effective
optical path length for the same beam path with the plasma contribution
removed.

The quantity applies to all plasma encountered along the complete
propagation path of a single interferometer beam, with distributed
contributions aggregated into one path-length difference. It has no local
spatial, species-resolved, or charge-state-resolved meaning. It excludes the
unvaried reference path length and is not the total [effective optical path
length](name:length_of_interferometer_beam) of the beam.

This variation is the optical-path quantity associated with the
interferometric phase shift and is used to relate the propagation path to
the [line-integrated electron number
density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density). It remains a
path-length difference and must not be identified with the electron column
density itself.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the plasma increases the effective optical
path length relative to the corresponding no-plasma reference path.

sources.leaf_definition: Optical path length variation due to the plasma

NAMES.name: wave_phase_of_wave_beam
NAMES.short:
Fringe-jump-corrected phase angle of a probing electromagnetic signal at a
selected wavelength, referenced to the channel’s defined launch phase.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the continuous phase angle of a probing electromagnetic
signal at one selected wavelength, with integer-cycle discontinuities caused
by fringe jumps removed. It represents the phase accumulated along the
signal’s propagation chord relative to the channel’s defined launch-phase
reference.

The corrected phase is related to the measured wrapped phase by

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{corr}} = \phi_{\mathrm{meas}} + 2\pi N_{\mathrm{fj}}
$$

where $\phi_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the fringe-jump-corrected phase,
$\phi_{\mathrm{meas}}$ is the measured wrapped phase, and $N_{\mathrm{fj}}$
is the signed integer number of full-cycle fringe-jump corrections. The
factor $2\pi$ represents one complete phase revolution.

The quantity applies to a single probing wavelength and represents the phase
accumulated over the complete propagation chord, rather than a local phase
at one point. It is referenced to the channel’s defined launch phase; it is
not an absolute electromagnetic phase and does not include an uncorrected
fringe discontinuity.

The corrected phase is the phase observable used to obtain the
[line-integrated electron number
density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density) through the
wavelength-dependent plasma refractive index. It is distinct from the
general [reference phase](name:reference_phase), which establishes a phase
origin without specifying fringe-jump correction or a propagation chord.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume averaged along a
complete plasma propagation chord, equal to the path integral divided by
chord length.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume averaged along a
complete propagation chord is the path-normalized continuum count density of
the unqualified free-electron population along that chord.

For local [electron density](name:electron_density) $n_e(l)$, the defining
relation is:

$$
\bar{n}_e = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_e(l)\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_e$ is the line-averaged electron density, $n_e(l)$ is the
local free-electron density at path coordinate $l$, $l$ is distance along
the complete propagation chord, and $L$ is the full chord length.

This quantity applies to the complete unqualified free-electron population
along the chord, aggregating all contributing free-electron populations
rather than selecting thermal or fast electrons. It is a path average over
the chord and is not a pointwise [electron density](name:electron_density)
or a line-integrated column density.

The numerator in the defining relation is the [line-integrated electron
number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density); dividing it
by the chord length produces this path-normalized quantity. The same
line-averaging construction applies to species-specific quantities such as
[line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), while
this quantity remains specific to free electrons.

NAMES.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless radial label that maps a physical measurement position to a
nested magnetic surface using the square root of normalized poloidal
magnetic flux.
NAMES.long:
The normalized poloidal flux coordinate at a measurement position assigns
the physical point to a nested closed magnetic surface through its radial
position between the magnetic axis and the last closed flux surface. It is
the pointwise value of the [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate) at that measurement
location.

The defining normalization is

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{meas}})=\sqrt{\frac{\psi(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{meas}})-\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}-\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}}$ is the normalized poloidal flux coordinate,
$\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{meas}}$ is the physical measurement position,
$\psi(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{meas}})$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at that
position, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at the
magnetic axis, and $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at
the last closed flux surface.

This quantity applies to one physical measurement position and has no
population or region aggregation: it is evaluated pointwise rather than
averaged along a path or over a region. It is a normalized surface label,
not a poloidal magnetic-flux value or a toroidal-flux coordinate.

The transformation preserves the parent coordinate's normalization: it is
zero at the magnetic axis and one at the last closed flux surface, with
intermediate values identifying nested surfaces between those boundaries.
