NAMES.name: electron_pressure
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Electron kinetic pressure is one-third of the trace of the velocity-space
stress, covering thermal, suprathermal, and combined populations.
NAMES.long:
Electron kinetic pressure is the isotropic scalar measure of momentum flux
generated by random electron motion about the population mean velocity. It
may describe a suprathermal component, a thermal component, or their
combined electron population.

The defining pressure is

$$
p_e = \frac{m_e}{3}\int \lvert \mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_e\rvert^2 f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_e$ is the electron kinetic pressure, $m_e$ is the electron mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is an individual electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the mean
velocity of the represented electron population, $f_e(\mathbf{v})$ is its
velocity distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

At parent scope, the quantity applies to a selected thermal or suprathermal
electron population or to their full aggregate. Aggregation is over the
represented electrons in velocity space, not over ion or neutral species;
the full aggregate combines disjoint thermal and suprathermal contributions.

This quantity is the trace-based scalar reduction of the electron kinetic
stress and does not specify a directional pressure-tensor component. An
anisotropic electron stress is therefore represented here only through its
trace, while ion pressure, neutral pressure, and individual tensor
components are excluded.

The [fast-electron pressure contribution](name:fast_electron_pressure) is
the suprathermal component within this common kinetic-pressure concept. The
[total electron pressure](name:total_electron_pressure) is the aggregate
over the designated thermal and suprathermal electron populations and equals
their sum when those components are disjoint.

NAMES.name: fast_electron_pressure
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Kinetic pressure associated with the fast electron population, retaining
directional momentum transport rather than imposing an isotropic thermal
approximation.
NAMES.long:
Fast electron pressure is the kinetic pressure-tensor contribution of the
suprathermal electron population, representing random electron momentum
transport carried by fast electrons.

For the fast-electron distribution function, its defining relation is

$$
\mathbf{P}_{e,f}=m_e\int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{e,f})(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{e,f})f_{e,f}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{e,f}$ is the fast-electron pressure tensor, $m_e$ is
electron mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{e,f}$ is the
mean velocity of the fast-electron population, $f_{e,f}(\mathbf{v})$ is its
velocity distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element.

The scope is the aggregate suprathermal electron population, including its
directional pressure response and excluding the bulk thermal-electron
contribution. It is not restricted to a single magnetic-field direction or
to an isotropic stress representation.

The directional projections of this quantity are represented by [parallel
fast electron pressure](name:parallel_fast_electron_pressure) and
[perpendicular fast electron
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_electron_pressure). Within the broader
[electron pressure](name:electron_pressure) concept, it supplies the
fast-population contribution; [total electron
pressure](name:total_electron_pressure) combines fast and thermal electron
contributions in the complete electron population.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the relevant pressure-tensor projection is
compressive rather than tensile.

NAMES.name: greenwald_density
NAMES.short:
Greenwald density is the empirical electron number-density limit associated
with a confined plasma, set by the magnitude of plasma current and the
effective minor radius. It is the density reference used by Greenwald
fractions, not the fraction itself.
NAMES.long:
Greenwald density is the empirical electron number-density limit associated
with a confined toroidal plasma. It is a global density reference for
proximity-to-limit quantities, not a measured local or averaged electron
density.

The Greenwald density is defined by scaling the magnitude of the plasma
current by the plasma cross-sectional area represented through the effective
minor radius:

$$
n_G = C_G \frac{\left|I_p\right|}{\pi a_\mathrm{eff}^2}
$$

where $n_G$ is the Greenwald density, $C_G$ is the Greenwald proportionality
constant, $I_p$ is the [plasma current](name:plasma_current), and
$a_\mathrm{eff}$ is the effective minor radius of the confined plasma
cross-section.

This quantity denotes the empirical limit density itself. It does not denote
a local electron density, a line-averaged electron density, a
volume-averaged electron density, or any normalized Greenwald fraction.

For Greenwald-fraction quantities, this density is the common denominator:
the [ratio of line-averaged electron density to Greenwald
density](name:ratio_of_line_averaged_electron_density_to_greenwald_density)
divides a specified line-averaged electron-density measure by $n_G$.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the helium-3 ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local helium-3 ion count per physical volume at that
location. It is summed over all helium-3 ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the helium-3 ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local helium-3 ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents helium-3 ions specifically, rather than neutral
helium-3, electrons, or another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{3,\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_3}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{3,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_3$ is the number of helium-3 ions, and $V$ is physical
volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete helium-3 ion population at that
location and is summed over all helium-3 ionic charge states; it is neither
a flux-surface or volume integral nor a neutral-helium or other-species
density.

This is the helium-3-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). The
unlocalized [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density) describes the same
charge-state-summed helium-3 ion population without this specified
magnetic-axis locus, while [helium-4 density at the magnetic
axis](name:helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis) represents the corresponding
density for a different helium isotope.

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the helium-4 ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local helium-4 ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all helium-4 ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the helium-4 ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local helium-4 ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all helium-4 ionic charge states. It represents
helium-4 ions specifically, rather than neutral helium, electrons, other
isotopes, or another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{ion}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the helium-4 ion number
density at the magnetic axis, $N_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{ion}}$ is the
number of helium-4 ions summed over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is
physical volume. The superscript $4$ identifies the helium isotope with four
nucleons.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete helium-4 ion population at that
location and is summed over all helium-4 ionic charge states; it is neither
a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density of neutral helium or another
isotope.

This is the helium-4-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis), whose
population is left unspecified at the parent level. It is distinguished from
[helium-3 density at the magnetic
axis](name:helium_3_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts helium-3 ions
rather than helium-4 ions.

NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the hydrogen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local hydrogen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all hydrogen ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the hydrogen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local hydrogen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all hydrogen ionic charge states. It represents
hydrogen ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutral hydrogen, or
another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{H}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the hydrogen-ion number density at
the magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the number of hydrogen ions summed
over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete hydrogen-ion population at that
location and is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor an electron or
neutral density.

This is the hydrogen-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [deuterium density at the magnetic
axis](name:deuterium_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts deuterium ions,
and from [hydrogenic density](name:hydrogenic_density), which aggregates
hydrogen-isotope populations rather than isolating hydrogen.

NAMES.name: ion_atomic_mass
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short:
Mass parameter assigned to a specified ion species, encoding its isotope and
setting the inertial scale for collisional and transport calculations.
NAMES.long:
Atomic mass is the intrinsic mass parameter assigned to one specified ion
species. It identifies the ion's isotope and provides the inertial scale
used in collisional and transport physics.

The mass is represented relative to the atomic mass unit by

$$
m_s = A_s m_u
$$

where $m_s$ is the atomic mass of the specified ion species, $A_s$ is its
relative atomic mass, and $m_u$ is the atomic mass unit.

The scope is one ion-species definition at a time. No aggregation over
separate ion species, charge states, or plasma populations is implied, and
the quantity does not represent a number density, mass density, or aggregate
plasma mass. This ion-specific form specializes [atomic
mass](name:atomic_mass) to ions, while [neutral species atomic
mass](name:neutral_species_atomic_mass) applies the same mass concept to
uncharged particle species.

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the iron ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local iron-ion count per physical volume at that location,
summed over all iron ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the iron ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local iron-ion count per physical volume at that location. It
represents iron ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutral iron, or
another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe,axis}}$ is the iron-ion number density at the magnetic
axis, $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the number of iron ions summed over all iron
ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete ionic iron population at that location,
with all iron charge states aggregated, and is neither a flux-surface or
volume integral nor a neutral-iron density.

This is the iron-specific realization of the population-independent [density
at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It is distinguished
from [hydrogen density at the magnetic
axis](name:hydrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts hydrogen ions,
and from [iron density at the internal transport
barrier](name:iron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), which is
evaluated on the flux surface assigned to that barrier rather than at the
magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the krypton ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local krypton-ion count per physical volume at that
location.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the krypton ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local krypton-ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents krypton ions specifically, summed over all ionic
charge states and excluding neutral krypton.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Kr}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr,axis}}$ is the krypton-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the number of krypton ions summed over
ionic charge states, $V$ is physical volume, and the subscript axis denotes
evaluation at the magnetic axis.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete krypton-ion population at that
location, with number density summed over all krypton ionic charge states;
it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density of neutral
krypton, electrons, or other ion species.

This is the krypton-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). The [neon
density at the magnetic axis](name:neon_density_at_magnetic_axis) has the
same local locus and charge-state-summed convention but counts neon ions
rather than krypton ions.

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the lithium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local lithium-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all lithium ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the lithium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local lithium-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all lithium ionic charge states. It represents ionized
lithium specifically, rather than electrons, neutral lithium, or another
plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\sum_{q\ge 1} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li,axis}}$ is the total lithium-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the number of lithium ions, $V$ is
physical volume, $q$ is the positive integer labeling a lithium ionic charge
state, and $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is the number density of lithium ions in
charge state $q$.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete ionized lithium population at that
location and uses a sum over all lithium ionic charge states, not a density
for one selected charge state or a sum over different chemical elements. It
is neither a flux-surface nor volume integral and excludes neutral lithium.

This is the lithium-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It has the
same local-density and magnetic-axis scope as [deuterium density at the
magnetic axis](name:deuterium_density_at_magnetic_axis), but counts lithium
ions rather than deuterium ions; unlike [electron density at the magnetic
axis](name:electron_density_at_magnetic_axis), it does not count electrons.

NAMES.name: loop_voltage_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short:
Toroidal electromotive force evaluated on the last closed flux surface that
drives the conventionally signed ohmic plasma current.
NAMES.long:
The loop voltage at the plasma boundary is the toroidal electromotive force
associated with the inductive electric field around the last closed
magnetic-flux surface. It is the net voltage available to drive the ohmic
component of the confined plasma current.

For a closed toroidal contour $C$ on the last closed flux surface, the loop
voltage is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{loop}} = \oint_C \mathbf{E} \cdot d\boldsymbol{\ell}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{loop}}$ is the loop voltage, $\mathbf{E}$ is the
electric-field vector, $d\boldsymbol{\ell}$ is the directed line element,
and $C$ is oriented in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. The
quantity is a contour-integrated scalar evaluated at the plasma boundary,
not a local electric-field component or an external-coil terminal voltage.

This boundary quantity represents the total loop voltage driving plasma
current, including the inductive contribution associated with changing
poloidal magnetic flux. It excludes no plasma-current-driving contribution
merely because it is externally generated; the narrower [external loop
voltage](name:external_loop_voltage) denotes only the externally generated
contribution and is therefore not equivalent to the total boundary loop
voltage.

The loop voltage is related to the ohmic plasma-current drive through the
toroidal component of the electric field and the plasma conductivity. The
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame uses $R$ for major radius,
$\phi$ for toroidal angle, and $Z$ for vertical height.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the electromotive force drives conventional
plasma current in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
counter-clockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the neon ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local neon-ion count per physical volume at that location,
summed over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the neon ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local neon-ion count per physical volume at that location,
summed over all neon ionic charge states. It represents neon ions
specifically, rather than neutral neon, electrons, or another plasma
population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne,axis}} = \sum_{q=1}^{Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne,axis}}$ is the total neon-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the number density of
neon ions with charge state $q$ at that location, $q$ is the positive ionic
charge-state index, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the atomic number of neon.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the neon-ion population at that location and is
summed over ionic charge states; neutral neon is excluded, and the quantity
is neither a flux-surface nor a volume integral.

This is the neon-specific realization of the population-independent [density
at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It has the same locus
and charge-state aggregation convention as [oxygen density at the magnetic
axis](name:oxygen_density_at_magnetic_axis), but counts neon ions rather
than oxygen ions.

NAMES.name: neutral_species_atomic_mass
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short:
Mass parameter assigned to a specified neutral particle species, encoding
its isotope or constituent composition for inertial and transport
calculations.
NAMES.long:
Atomic mass is the intrinsic mass parameter assigned to one specified
neutral particle species. It identifies an isotope for an atomic neutral or
the constituent composition for a molecular or compound neutral, and
provides the inertial scale used in collisional and transport physics.

The mass is represented relative to the atomic mass unit by

$$
m_s = A_s m_u
$$

where $m_s$ is the atomic mass of the specified neutral species, $A_s$ is
its relative atomic mass, and $m_u$ is the atomic mass unit.

The scope is one neutral species definition at a time. For an atomic
neutral, the definition identifies its isotope; for a molecular or compound
neutral, it includes the masses of its constituents. No aggregation over
separate species or plasma populations is implied, and this quantity is not
a number density, particle count, or aggregate plasma mass.

This neutral-specific quantity is an instance of the broader [atomic
mass](name:atomic_mass) concept. The corresponding [ion atomic
mass](name:ion_atomic_mass) applies the same mass definition to an ion
species rather than a neutral particle species.

NAMES.name: neutral_temperature
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short:
Translational kinetic temperature, expressed as energy per particle, of a
neutral population, based on random translational motion after removal of
bulk flow and averaged over represented charge states when applicable.
NAMES.long:
The translational kinetic temperature quantifies the random motion of a
neutral population after its bulk translational motion has been removed. It
describes translational kinetic energy and excludes energy associated with
internal excitation or other internal quantum states.

For an isotropic translational distribution, the energy-equivalent
temperature is defined by

$$
T_n = \frac{2}{3}\left\langle \frac{1}{2}m_n\left|\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_n\right|^2 \right\rangle
$$

where $T_n$ is the neutral translational temperature, $m_n$ is the mass of a
neutral particle, $\mathbf{v}$ is its velocity, $\mathbf{u}_n$ is the bulk
translational velocity of the neutral population, and the angle brackets
denote an average over the selected particles.

The quantity applies to the selected neutral population without restricting
it to cold or energetic particles or to a particular spatial region. When
multiple charge states are represented, it is the density-weighted mean over
all represented charge states rather than their sum. The unqualified
quantity has no spatial aggregation;
[volume_averaged_neutral_temperature](name:volume_averaged_neutral_temperature)
is the corresponding quantity after volume averaging inside the last closed
flux surface.

The [cold_neutral_temperature](name:cold_neutral_temperature) and
[hot_neutral_temperature](name:hot_neutral_temperature) names restrict this
common translational-temperature definition to distinct neutral populations.
In contrast,
[neutral_internal_state_temperature](name:neutral_internal_state_temperature)
restricts the population to a specified internal quantum or excitation
state.

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the nitrogen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local nitrogen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all nitrogen ionic charge states and excluding neutral
nitrogen.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the nitrogen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local nitrogen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all nitrogen ionic charge states. It represents
nitrogen ions specifically, rather than neutral nitrogen, electrons, or
other ion species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{N,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{N,ion}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{N,axis}}$ is the nitrogen-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{N,ion}}$ is the total number of nitrogen ions
summed over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete nitrogen-ion population at that
location, uses a sum over nitrogen ionic charge states, and excludes neutral
nitrogen; it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density of
another species.

This is the nitrogen-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It follows
the same charge-state-summed convention as [helium-4 density at the magnetic
axis](name:helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis), while differing in the ion
species counted.

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the oxygen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local oxygen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all oxygen ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the oxygen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local oxygen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all oxygen ionic charge states. It represents oxygen
ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutral oxygen, or another plasma
population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{O,axis}} = \left.\sum_q \frac{dN_{\mathrm{O},q}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O,axis}}$ is the oxygen-ion number density at the magnetic
axis, $q$ is an oxygen ionic charge state, $N_{\mathrm{O},q}$ is the number
of oxygen ions in charge state $q$, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the oxygen ion population and is summed over all
oxygen ionic charge states; neutral oxygen is excluded. It is a local
density, not a flux-surface or volume integral.

This is the oxygen-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [neon density at the magnetic
axis](name:neon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which applies the same local,
charge-state-summed convention to neon ions.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_line_averaged_electron_density_to_greenwald_density
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless Greenwald fraction comparing the electron number density
averaged along a plasma chord with the empirical density limit set by plasma
current and effective minor radius.
NAMES.long:
The Greenwald fraction measures the proximity of a confined plasma's
line-averaged electron density to its empirical Greenwald density limit.

It is defined by:

$$
f_G = \frac{\bar{n}_e}{n_G}
$$

where $f_G$ is the Greenwald fraction, $\bar{n}_e$ is the [line-averaged
electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), and $n_G$ is the
[Greenwald density](name:greenwald_density) determined from the
plasma-current magnitude and effective minor radius.

The numerator represents the electron population averaged along a plasma
chord; the denominator is the empirical density reference for the confined
plasma. This quantity is a global normalized ratio, not a local electron
density, a density limit itself, or an average over charge states or spatial
regions.

The fraction is the direct normalization of line-averaged electron density
by Greenwald density: values near unity indicate proximity to the empirical
reference limit, while values above or below unity indicate a line-averaged
density respectively above or below that reference.

NAMES.name: safety_factor_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short:
Signed field-line winding ratio evaluated on the magnetic flux surface
designated as the internal transport barrier, giving toroidal turns per
poloidal circuit.
NAMES.long:
The safety factor at the internal transport barrier is the signed helical
winding of magnetic field lines on the flux surface designated as the
barrier. It counts toroidal turns per poloidal circuit at that specific
locus.

The defining flux-increment relation is:

$$
q_{\mathrm{ITB}} = \left.\frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}}{d\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}}\right|_{\mathrm{ITB}}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the safety factor evaluated on the
internal-transport-barrier flux surface, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is toroidal
magnetic flux, $\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is poloidal magnetic flux, and the
subscript $\mathrm{ITB}$ denotes evaluation on that designated surface.

This quantity applies only to the flux surface associated with the internal
transport barrier. It is a single flux-surface value, with no averaging or
aggregation over neighboring surfaces, plasma volume, or other regions
implied.

It is distinct from safety-factor values evaluated at other loci, such as
the [safety factor at the pedestal top](name:safety_factor_at_pedestal_top),
and it does not represent a general radial profile or a value at the
magnetic axis or plasma boundary.

The [safety factor](name:safety_factor) is the corresponding
locus-independent flux-surface quantity; this name specializes it by fixing
the evaluation surface. The [rotational
transform](name:rotational_transform) uses the reciprocal field-line winding
convention, counting poloidal turns per toroidal circuit.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the toroidal and poloidal flux increments
have the same sign, taking $\phi$ as the toroidal angle in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius, $Z$ the vertical
height, and the positive poloidal circuit defined by increasing
$\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}$.

NAMES.name: temperature_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.short:
Energy-equivalent temperature scale at the magnetic axis, representing
either particle thermal energy or radiation brightness.
NAMES.long:
Temperature at the magnetic axis is an energy-equivalent measure of a
thermal state or radiation field evaluated at the magnetic axis. It provides
a shared parent concept for kinetic temperatures and brightness
temperatures, which need not represent the same underlying physical state.

For a temperature parameter expressed as an energy-equivalent quantity, the
defining conversion is:

$$
\Theta = k_{\mathrm B} T
$$

where $\Theta$ is the energy-equivalent temperature, $T$ is the underlying
thermodynamic or brightness-temperature parameter, and $k_{\mathrm B}$ is
Boltzmann's constant. This conversion does not imply that a radiation
brightness temperature equals the local kinetic temperature.

The quantity is evaluated at the magnetic axis, the innermost location of
nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces. The parent name specifies no
particle species, charge-state aggregation, radiation band, or
population-weighting convention; it is therefore neither a charge-state sum
nor an all-plasma aggregate by itself.

The [electron temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) is the kinetic-temperature
specialization for electrons. The [radiative temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:radiative_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) is the
brightness-temperature specialization for electron-cyclotron radiation and
is not necessarily the local kinetic electron temperature. Unlike [plasma
temperature](name:plasma_temperature), this parent does not require an
effective fluid or magnetohydrodynamic aggregation.

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Thermal energy per particle of the electron population, expressed as an
energy-equivalent temperature and evaluated at the magnetic axis.
NAMES.long:
Thermal energy per particle of the electron population, expressed as an
energy-equivalent temperature and evaluated at the magnetic axis. The
magnetic axis is the degenerate innermost magnetic surface of the
equilibrium, where the gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux vanishes;
evaluation at this locus does not imply that the electron temperature has an
extremum there.

For a thermal electron population with a well-defined absolute thermodynamic
temperature, the energy-equivalent electron temperature is defined by:

$$
T_e = k_\mathrm{B}\,\Theta_e
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature expressed as energy per particle,
$\Theta_e$ is the absolute thermodynamic temperature of the electrons, and
$k_\mathrm{B}$ is the Boltzmann constant.

This quantity applies specifically to the electron population at the
magnetic axis and is an intensive, per-particle quantity rather than a
charge-state sum, volume average, or volume-integrated electron energy. It
excludes ion temperatures, radiative temperature-equivalent scales, and the
total thermal energy content of the electron population.

It is the electron-specific member of the broader [temperature at the
magnetic axis](name:temperature_at_magnetic_axis), which also encompasses
other populations and radiative temperature interpretations. The
corresponding electron temperature at another locus is [electron temperature
at the outboard midplane](name:electron_temperature_at_outboard_midplane),
while [thermal electron energy](name:thermal_electron_energy) denotes an
integrated energy content rather than this local temperature.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_pressure_at_post_sawtooth_crash
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Isotropic kinetic pressure produced by random motion of bulk thermal
electrons, evaluated in the plasma state immediately after a sawtooth crash.
NAMES.long:
Thermal electron pressure is the isotropic scalar stress contribution
produced by random motion of the bulk electron population in the designated
post-sawtooth-crash plasma state. It represents the thermal electron
contribution rather than the pressure of the full electron population.

For an isotropic thermal population, the pressure is defined by

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{2}{3} n_{e,\mathrm{th}}\langle E_{e,\mathrm{rand}}\rangle
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal electron pressure,
$n_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the number density of thermal electrons, and $\langle
E_{e,\mathrm{rand}}\rangle$ is their mean random kinetic energy; the
subscripts $e$ and $\mathrm{th}$ identify electrons and the thermal
population, respectively.

The quantity applies only to bulk thermal electrons and is evaluated in the
plasma state immediately following a sawtooth crash. It is an isotropic
scalar contribution, aggregated over the included thermal electrons, and
excludes fast or otherwise nonthermal electron contributions.

It is the thermal component of [total electron
pressure](name:total_electron_pressure), which combines thermal and
suprathermal electron contributions. A fast-particle pressure quantity such
as [fast particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure) represents a
distinct nonthermal population and must not be included in this thermal
contribution.

NAMES.name: total_electron_pressure
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Kinetic pressure associated with the entire electron population, combining
thermal and suprathermal contributions in the isotropic electron stress.
NAMES.long:
Total electron pressure is the isotropic kinetic part of the electron
pressure tensor, representing random electron momentum transport for the
complete electron population.

For the combined electron distribution function, its defining relation is

$$
p_e = \frac{m_e}{3} \int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_e|^2 f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_e$ is total electron pressure, $m_e$ is electron mass, $\mathbf{v}$
is electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is mean electron velocity, and
$f_e(\mathbf{v})$ is the combined electron velocity distribution function
normalized so its velocity integral gives the electron number density.

The aggregation includes both bulk thermal and suprathermal electrons and
applies across core, edge, and scrape-off-layer plasma. It excludes
anisotropic stress components and is not restricted to the thermal electron
population alone.

This quantity makes the total aggregation explicit within [electron
pressure](name:electron_pressure): it is the sum of the thermal contribution
and the [fast electron pressure](name:fast_electron_pressure) contribution.
The parent name denotes the same isotropic pressure concept without
requiring the total qualifier.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the isotropic electron stress is compressive
rather than tensile.

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the tritium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tritium-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all tritium ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the tritium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tritium-ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents tritium ions specifically, rather than electrons,
other ion species, neutral tritium, or another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{T,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{T}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{T,axis}}$ is the tritium-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the number of tritium ions, and $V$ is
physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete tritium-ion population at that location
and is summed over all tritium ionic charge states; neutral tritium is
excluded. It is neither a flux-surface nor a volume integral.

This is the tritium-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [tritium density at the plasma
boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary), which describes the same
charge-state aggregation at the plasma boundary rather than at the magnetic
axis.

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the tungsten ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tungsten-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all positive ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the tungsten ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tungsten-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all positive ionic charge states. It represents
tungsten ions specifically, rather than electrons, other ion species, or
neutral tungsten.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
n_{W,\mathrm{axis}} = \sum_{q=1}^{q_{\max}} n_{W^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{W,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the tungsten ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $W$ denotes tungsten, $q$ is the positive integer ionic
charge state, $q_{\max}$ is the highest included tungsten charge state, and
$n_{W^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the number density of tungsten ions in charge
state $q$ at the magnetic axis.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete positively charged tungsten-ion
population at that location, summed over charge states; it is neither a
flux-surface or volume integral nor the density of neutral tungsten or one
individual charge state.

This is the tungsten-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [xenon density at the magnetic
axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which applies the same local,
charge-state-summed convention to xenon ions instead of tungsten ions.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short:
Particle number density of the xenon ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local xenon-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all xenon ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the xenon ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local xenon-ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents xenon ions specifically, rather than neutral xenon,
electrons, or another ion species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe,axis}}$ is the xenon-ion number density at the magnetic
axis, $N_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the number of xenon ions summed over all xenon
ionization states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete xenon-ion population at that location
and is charge-state-summed; it is neither a density of neutral xenon nor an
integral over a flux surface or volume.

This is the xenon-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It is the
on-axis counterpart of [xenon density](name:xenon_density), which applies at
a general plasma location, and it is distinguished from [argon density at
the magnetic axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts a
different ion species.

NAMES.name: fast_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the local fast
electron population, excluding the bulk thermal Maxwellian component.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the local fast
electron population is the local continuum count density of electrons not
bound to atoms, molecules, or ions that belong to the nonthermal
fast-electron component.

For the fast-electron distribution, the defining relation is:

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local fast-electron number
density, $f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})$ is the fast-electron
velocity distribution, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron
velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the volume element in velocity space.

This quantity applies only to the local nonthermal fast or suprathermal
electron population. The bulk thermal Maxwellian electron component is
excluded, and no aggregation along a chord or over a plasma volume is
performed; the quantity is a local component density rather than a fraction
of the total population.

The parent [electron density](name:electron_density) denotes the unqualified
local free-electron density. The [thermal electron
density](name:thermal_electron_density) describes the complementary bulk
thermal component, while the [total electron
density](name:total_electron_density) combines the thermal and fast
components when they are resolved separately.

NAMES.name: parallel_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Signed parallel magnetic-field component of the local total induction,
resolved along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction rather than a
cylindrical axis.
NAMES.long:
The parallel magnetic field $B_\parallel$ is the signed component of the
local total [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) resolved along the
local equilibrium magnetic-field direction. It represents directional field
strength rather than the full magnetic-induction vector or its magnitude.

The parallel component is defined by

$$
B_\parallel = \mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm eq}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the local total magnetic induction,
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm eq}$ is the unit vector in the direction of the local
equilibrium magnetic field, and $B_\parallel$ is the resulting field-aligned
component.

This quantity is defined locally using the total magnetic induction and the
local equilibrium-field direction. It has no restriction to a particular
plasma source, vacuum source, physical region, or species; its aggregation
convention is a pointwise directional projection, not a sum or average over
components, modes, populations, or spatial regions.

Unlike the [radial magnetic field](name:radial_magnetic_field), [toroidal
magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), and [vertical magnetic
field](name:vertical_magnetic_field), it is resolved along the local
equilibrium field rather than along an axis of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height. Unlike the [parallel wave magnetic
field](name:parallel_wave_magnetic_field), it is not restricted to an
oscillatory wave perturbation. It is the field-aligned projection of the
parent [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field).
NAMES.sign:
Positive when the local total magnetic induction has a
component in the direction of the local equilibrium magnetic-field unit
vector.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_line_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_line_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless line-averaged protium fraction among hydrogenic ions, obtained
by dividing the protium density by the total hydrogenic density along the
same chord.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the fraction of hydrogenic ion content carried by protium
along a specified chord through the plasma. It is a ratio of consistently
line-averaged densities, rather than a local fraction or a volume-averaged
fraction.

$$
f_{\rm H}^{\rm line} = \frac{\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}}{\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}+\bar{n}_{\rm D}^{\rm line}+\bar{n}_{\rm T}^{\rm line}}
$$

where $f_{\rm H}^{\rm line}$ is the line-averaged protium fraction,
$\bar{n}_{\rm H}^{\rm line}$ is the line-averaged protium-ion number
density, $\bar{n}_{\rm D}^{\rm line}$ is the corresponding deuterium-ion
number density, and $\bar{n}_{\rm T}^{\rm line}$ is the corresponding
tritium-ion number density. The symbols H, D, and T denote protium,
deuterium, and tritium, respectively.

The quantity applies to the hydrogenic ion population along one common chord
and aggregates the isotope densities through the total hydrogenic
denominator. Neutral atomic hydrogen and non-hydrogenic species are
excluded. The numerator is the [line-averaged hydrogen
density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), while the denominator is the
[total hydrogenic density](name:total_hydrogenic_density) under the same
line-averaging convention.

This ratio differs from the [ratio of volume-averaged hydrogen density to
volume-averaged total hydrogenic
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density),
because the latter uses volume-averaged rather than chord-averaged isotope
densities.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_total_ion_density_to_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless ratio of total ion number density, summed over all ion species
and charge states, to local electron number density including thermal and
non-thermal electrons.
NAMES.long:
The ion-to-electron density ratio compares the total particle count density
of ions with the local particle count density of electrons. It is a
composition and quasi-neutrality indicator based on particle counts, not on
charge-weighted positive and negative densities.

$$
\mathcal{R}_{i/e} = \frac{n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}}{n_e}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{i/e}$ is the ion-to-electron density ratio,
$n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the [total ion
density](name:total_ion_number_density) summed over all represented ion
species and charge states, including thermal and non-thermal ions, and $n_e$
is the local electron number density including thermal and non-thermal
electrons.

The quantity applies locally at a plasma point and uses total aggregation in
the numerator rather than a species-specific or charge-state-resolved ion
density. It is not a charge density ratio and does not weight ions by their
charge; consequently, it is distinct from [effective
charge](name:effective_charge), which characterizes a charge-weighted ionic
mixture.

The ratio is obtained by dividing the aggregated total ion density by the
electron density, so it equals unity when those two particle number
densities are equal. Its departure from unity describes the difference
between total ion and electron counts and must not be interpreted alone as a
direct charge-neutrality residual.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the local thermal
electron population, excluding fast and suprathermal electron contributions.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the local thermal
electron population is the local continuum count density of electrons not
bound to atoms, molecules, or ions that belong to the bulk Maxwellian
electron component.

For the thermal electron distribution, the defining relation is:

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int f_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local thermal electron number
density, $f_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})$ is the thermal-electron
velocity distribution, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron
velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the volume element in velocity space.

This quantity applies only to the local bulk thermal electron population.
Fast and suprathermal electrons are excluded, and the quantity is neither a
chord average nor a volume average. The parent [electron
density](name:electron_density) denotes the unqualified local free-electron
density without this population restriction.

The complete local [total electron density](name:total_electron_density) is
the sum of this thermal component and the corresponding [fast electron
density](name:fast_electron_density) when those components are resolved
separately.

NAMES.name: time_derivative_of_derivative_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_volume_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short:
Temporal change of the geometric volume derivative with respect to the
dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate for each nested magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the temporal rate of change of the volume change associated
with an increment of dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate on a nested
magnetic flux surface.

It is defined by

$$
\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}\right)\right|_{\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}
$$

where $V$ is the cumulative volume enclosed by the flux surface,
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the dimensionful toroidal flux coordinate labeling
that surface, and $t$ is time. The outer derivative is taken at fixed
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$, following the corresponding moving flux surface as
the equilibrium evolves.

The quantity applies to an individual nested magnetic flux surface and has
no species, population, or source-process weighting. It is a temporal
derivative of a geometric metric coefficient, not the enclosed volume
itself, a volume integral, a flux-surface average, or an aggregation over
multiple surfaces.

It is the time-transformed counterpart of the [volume derivative with
respect to toroidal flux
coordinate](name:derivative_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_volume_of_flux_surface):
the linked quantity is the inner derivative $\partial V/\partial
\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$, while this quantity applies the outer
partial-time-derivative operator to it.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short:
Non-negative radius-like label of the nested magnetic flux surface
coinciding with the internal transport barrier, derived from enclosed
toroidal magnetic flux rather than geometric distance.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal-flux coordinate at the internal transport barrier is the
non-negative, radius-like label of the nested magnetic flux surface on which
the barrier is located. It identifies the barrier by magnetic-surface
position and is not a direct geometric distance.

The coordinate is defined from the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux:

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor}} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal-flux coordinate,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the
associated magnetic surface, $B_0$ is the positive reference toroidal
magnetic field, and $\pi$ is the mathematical circle constant.

The locus is the internal transport barrier, represented as a particular
nested magnetic flux surface rather than the entire plasma or a finite
transport-barrier region. This quantity has no species or charge-state
aggregation and is not a spatial average or an integral over a region.

It is the locus-specific evaluation of the parent [toroidal flux
coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate). Unlike the [normalized
toroidal-flux coordinate at the internal transport
barrier](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier),
it retains the radius-like coordinate scale rather than applying boundary
normalization.

NAMES.name: total_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the complete local
population, combining thermal and fast electrons rather than selecting one
population component.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the complete local
electron population is the local continuum count density of electrons not
bound to atoms, molecules, or ions, including both thermal and fast
nonthermal contributions.

The complete local electron density is defined by:

$$
n_e^{\mathrm{total}} = n_e^{\mathrm{thermal}} + n_e^{\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $n_e^{\mathrm{total}}$ is the complete local free-electron number
density, $n_e^{\mathrm{thermal}}$ is the density of the local thermal
electron population represented by [thermal electron
density](name:thermal_electron_density), and $n_e^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
density of the local fast, nonthermal electron population represented by
[fast electron density](name:fast_electron_density).

This quantity applies locally to the full free-electron population and is
aggregated over its thermal and fast components. It excludes electrons bound
in atoms, molecules, or ions, and it is not restricted to either population
component. It is also distinct from [line-averaged electron
density](name:line_averaged_electron_density) and [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), which apply spatial
averaging rather than a local evaluation.

As the complete-population form of [electron
density](name:electron_density), it includes both thermal and nonthermal
contributions. Integrating this local quantity over a specified plasma
volume gives [volume-integrated total electron density], whereas the
component names retain only one electron population.

NAMES.name: total_plasma_pressure
NAMES.short:
Total plasma pressure is the isotropic kinetic pressure summed over all
represented plasma particle species and populations for equilibrium force
balance.
NAMES.long:
Total plasma pressure is the isotropic kinetic pressure summed over all
represented plasma particle species and populations in a fluid or
magnetohydrodynamic description. It represents the aggregate equilibrium
mechanical stress of the included particle populations, rather than a
pressure perturbation.

The total pressure is defined by the isotropic part of the aggregate kinetic
pressure tensor:

$$
p_{\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s p_s
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total plasma pressure,
$\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the combined kinetic pressure tensor of the
represented plasma particle populations, $\operatorname{tr}$ denotes the
tensor trace, $s$ indexes those species and populations, and $p_s$ is the
isotropic kinetic-pressure contribution from population $s$.

The quantity applies locally to the equilibrium plasma and aggregates all
represented kinetic particle contributions, including thermal and nonthermal
populations. The total qualifier denotes summation over the included
populations; it does not denote normalization, volume integration, or
addition of magnetic pressure.

It excludes magnetic pressure, dynamic ram pressure, anisotropic
pressure-tensor components, and first-order pressure perturbations. [Plasma
pressure](name:plasma_pressure) is the corresponding unqualified equilibrium
kinetic-pressure concept, while [thermal plasma
pressure](name:thermal_plasma_pressure) restricts the aggregation to thermal
electron and ion populations and [perturbed plasma
pressure](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure) describes a first-order variation
about equilibrium.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_effective_charge
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless volume-averaged effective ionic charge of a plasma mixture,
formed by averaging the local second ionic charge moment normalized by
free-electron density over the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged effective ionic charge is the effective charge of the
complete ion mixture after spatially averaging the local charge-weighted
ionic charge moment over the confined plasma volume.

The defining relation is

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff},V} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff},V}$ is the volume-averaged effective charge,
$Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [effective
charge](name:effective_charge), $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume,
$\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The average applies to the complete included ion mixture at every position,
with ionic contributions summed over all represented species and charge
states. It covers the confined plasma volume and is not restricted to one
species, one charge state, one region, or one flux surface; it is distinct
from an ordinary ion charge average.

This quantity is the volume-averaged counterpart of [effective
charge](name:effective_charge). It differs from [flux-surface-averaged
effective charge at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary),
which averages the local effective charge over a boundary surface, and from
[volume-averaged ion charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge), which
represents an ordinary ion charge number rather than the second charge
moment normalized by free-electron density.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume averaged over the
plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, giving the global
mean free-electron density.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume averaged over the
plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface is the global mean of
the unqualified free-electron density.

For local [electron density](name:electron_density) $n_e(\mathbf{x})$, the
defining relation is:

$$
\langle n_e\rangle_{\rm LCFS} = \frac{1}{V_{\rm LCFS}}\int_{V_{\rm LCFS}} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\langle n_e\rangle_{\rm LCFS}$ is the volume-averaged electron
density, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local free-electron number density at
spatial position $\mathbf{x}$, $V_{\rm LCFS}$ is the plasma volume enclosed
by the last closed flux surface, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is a differential volume
element.

The average includes the complete unqualified free-electron population
within the last-closed-flux-surface volume and is not restricted to thermal
or fast electrons. It is a global volume mean rather than a local value and
excludes plasma volume outside that boundary; unlike [line-averaged electron
density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), it is not averaged along a
chord.

This quantity is the volume-averaging transformation of [electron
density](name:electron_density). It provides the common denominator for
volume-averaged elemental abundance ratios, such as the [volume-averaged
argon-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
whose numerator and denominator are averaged over the same plasma volume.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Elemental abundance ratio of argon nuclei to free electrons inside the last
closed flux surface, formed from the corresponding volume-averaged
densities. The argon population is summed over all argon ion charge states
and excludes neutral argon.
NAMES.long:
Elemental abundance ratio of argon nuclei to free electrons inside the last
closed flux surface is the confined-plasma composition fraction obtained by
normalizing the volume-averaged argon density to the volume-averaged
electron density. The argon population is the species-level ion population
summed over all argon ion charge states.

The ratio is defined as the quotient of the corresponding volume-averaged
densities:

$$
C_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}
$$

where $C_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is this argon-to-electron abundance ratio, $\langle
n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged argon-ion number
density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the
[volume-averaged electron number
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and $V$ denotes the
confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface.

The scope is the confined plasma population inside the last closed flux
surface, with the same volume-averaging operation applied to the argon and
electron densities before forming the quotient. It excludes neutral argon,
is not charge-state-resolved, and is a ratio of volume averages rather than
the volume average of a local argon-to-electron density ratio.

This quantity is related to [argon_density](name:argon_density) as its
volume-averaged, electron-normalized elemental abundance;
[argon_density](name:argon_density) denotes the argon density before
normalization to the electron population.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless volume-averaged deuterium abundance ratio is the quotient of
the volume-averaged deuterium ion number density and the volume-averaged
electron number density over the same plasma volume. The deuterium numerator
is charge-state-summed over positive atomic ion charge states and excludes
neutral or molecular deuterium.
NAMES.long:
Dimensionless volume-averaged deuterium abundance ratio is the
electron-density-normalized abundance of deuterium ions in a specified
plasma volume. It is the quotient of the [volume-averaged deuterium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) and the [volume-averaged
electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) evaluated over that
same volume.

The ratio is defined by the quotient of volume averages:

$$
f_{D,V} = \frac{\langle n_D \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{D,V}$ is this abundance ratio, $n_D$ is the [deuterium
density](name:deuterium_density), $n_e$ is the electron density, $\langle
n_D \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is
the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and the subscript $V$
denotes averaging over the common plasma volume.

The numerator is the volume average of deuterium ion number density summed
over all positive atomic ion charge states. It excludes neutral deuterium
atoms, molecular deuterium, and deuterium bound in non-ion populations. The
aggregation convention is a quotient of two volume-averaged densities, not
the volume average of the pointwise ratio $n_D/n_e$.

For non-negative number densities and positive $\langle n_e \rangle_V$,
$f_{D,V}$ is non-negative. It is not the fraction of deuterium among all
fuel nuclei and does not represent the absolute deuterium particle
inventory. It differs from the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium abundance
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which uses the combined deuterium-tritium numerator, while this quantity
uses deuterium alone.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density divided by volume-averaged
electron density for the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species,
treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density divided by volume-averaged
electron density for the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species,
treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species, is the
electron-density-normalized abundance of that fuel species. It compares the
fuel-ion population with the electron population after each density is
averaged over the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined by:

$$
\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}}
\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), $\langle n_e
\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the
local number density of the combined deuterium-tritium effective species,
$n_e$ is the local electron number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$
denotes averaging over the common plasma volume $V$.

The scope is the plasma volume common to numerator and denominator; the
value is a ratio of two volume averages, not the volume average of a
pointwise density ratio. The numerator is a species-level extensive density
for the effective deuterium-tritium fuel species and is summed over all
charge states before averaging. It includes only that fuel species and
excludes helium ash, impurity ions, and separate isotope-composition ratios
such as the [tritium-to-deuterium density
ratio](name:ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density).

Equivalently, this quantity is the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density) normalized by the
[volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density);
it is a normalized ratio, not a derivative of either density. When the
combined deuterium-tritium density is resolved into deuterium and tritium
contributions over the same volume and denominator, it equals the sum of the
[volume-averaged deuterium-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density)
and the [volume-averaged tritium-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless composition ratio comparing the charge-state-summed helium-3
ion density averaged over the confined plasma volume with the electron
density averaged over the same volume. It is the helium-3 average divided by
the electron average.
NAMES.long:
Dimensionless composition ratio comparing the charge-state-summed helium-3
ion density averaged over the confined plasma volume with the electron
density averaged over the same volume. It is the helium-3 average divided by
the electron average and represents the global helium-3 ion composition
relative to electrons.

The ratio is defined by applying the volume average separately to each
density over the same confined plasma volume before division:

$$
r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e} =
\frac{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV}{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV}
$$

where $r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e}$ is this composition ratio,
$n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local helium-3 ion number density
summed over all charged ionization states, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local
electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position, $dV$ is the volume
element, and $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume, with the same symbol
denoting its volume measure in the normalization factors.

The scope is a species-level, volume-averaged, confined-plasma composition
ratio. The helium-3 population includes charged helium-3 ions summed over
charge states and excludes neutral helium-3 atoms; the electron population
is the corresponding electron population in the same confined volume. No
particular time within an evolution is part of the quantity definition.

This quantity is not the confined-volume average of the local ratio
$n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}/n_e$; it equals that average only for special spatial
distributions. Its numerator is the [volume-averaged helium-3
density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density), and its denominator is the
[volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density).
The [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density)
is the analogous isotope composition ratio for helium-4.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Helium-4 abundance ratio formed from mean densities inside the last closed
flux surface, comparing the charge-state-summed helium-4 ion density with
the electron density after each density is volume averaged.
NAMES.long:
Helium-4 abundance ratio formed from mean densities inside the last closed
flux surface is the quotient of the volume-averaged helium-4 ion number
density and the volume-averaged electron number density. It is a global
isotope-abundance measure for ionized helium-4 relative to electrons in the
plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface.

The ratio is defined from independent volume averages over the same enclosed
plasma volume:

$$
f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}, \qquad \langle n_s\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{LCFS}}\int_{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} n_s(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ is this helium-4 abundance ratio, the
superscript $V$ denotes formation from volume averages, $\langle
n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged helium-4
density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is
the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the
local number density of species $s$ at position $\mathbf{x}$,
$V_\mathrm{LCFS}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux
surface, and $dV$ is an element of that volume. For $s={}^4\mathrm{He}$,
$n_s$ is the local helium-4 ion number density summed over all ion charge
states; for $s=e$, $n_s$ is the local electron number density.

The semantic scope is species-level helium-4 ion density inside the last
closed flux surface. The helium-4 numerator is summed over all ion charge
states before averaging, while neutral helium-4 atoms and helium isotopes
other than helium-4 are excluded. Because the numerator and denominator are
averaged separately, this quantity is not the volume average of the local
ratio $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}/n_e$.

For fully stripped helium-4 ions in a quasi-neutral plasma, $2
f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ represents the helium-4 ion contribution to the
electron charge balance, apart from contributions of other ions and
departures from full stripping. The isotope analog is [ratio of
volume-averaged helium-3 density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
and the analogous elemental abundance quantity is [ratio of volume-averaged
neon density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).
It is related to [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 ion density to electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density)
by the shared helium-4 numerator species, while this name explicitly
normalizes by the independently volume-averaged electron density.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short:
Ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density
is the volume-averaged tritium number density, summed over all charge
states, divided by the volume-averaged electron number density.
NAMES.long:
Ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density
is the volume-averaged tritium number density divided by the volume-averaged
electron number density. It expresses the tritium contribution to plasma
composition relative to the electron population after both densities have
been averaged over the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined as:

$$
f_{T/e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_T \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{T/e}^{V}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_T \rangle_V$ is the
[volume-averaged tritium density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density),
$\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_T$ is the local [tritium
density](name:tritium_density), $n_e$ is the local [electron
density](name:electron_density), and $\langle q\rangle_V$ denotes
$V^{-1}\int_V q\,dV$ for scalar field $q$ over the common plasma volume $V$.

The scope is the specified plasma volume and the particle populations
contained in that volume. The tritium density is a species-level per-volume
amount and is therefore summed over all tritium charge states before volume
averaging. The definition contains no selection by the time of peak electron
density or by any other operating condition.

This quantity is the ratio of volume averages, not the volume average of the
local ratio $n_T/n_e$, and it is not normalized to the total hydrogenic-fuel
density. It is the tritium-only counterpart of the [ratio of volume-averaged
deuterium-tritium density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which uses the combined deuterium-plus-tritium numerator; it also differs
from the local [ratio of tritium density to electron density].

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_electron_temperature
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short:
Thermal energy of the bulk electron population expressed as an
energy-equivalent temperature, averaged over the confined plasma volume
inside the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged electron temperature is the energy-equivalent measure of the
mean random kinetic energy of the bulk electron population, averaged over
the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.

It is defined by the volume-weighted mean of the local electron temperature:

$$
\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} T_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_e\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged electron temperature,
$T_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron temperature at position
$\mathbf{x}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last
closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the differential volume element.

This is an intensive volume-weighted mean for the bulk electron population,
not a sum or a volume-integrated energy. It excludes ion populations and
does not itself represent the total electron thermal energy.

The quantity is the volume-averaged form of local [electron
temperature](name:electron_temperature). It uses volume weighting throughout
the confined plasma, unlike [line-averaged electron
temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature), which averages along
a specified plasma chord. It is distinct from [thermal electron
energy](name:thermal_electron_energy), which represents an extensive
volume-integrated energy content rather than an intensive temperature.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature
NAMES.short:
Dimensionless electron-temperature peaking ratio comparing the magnetic-axis
temperature with the volume-averaged temperature inside the last closed flux
surface.
NAMES.long:
The electron-temperature peaking ratio measures central thermal
concentration by comparing the electron temperature at the magnetic axis
with its volume average inside the last closed flux surface.

$$
P_{T_e} = \frac{T_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}})}{\langle T_e\rangle_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}} = \frac{T_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}})}{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{LCFS}}^{-1} \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} T_e(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}^3\mathbf{x}}
$$

Here, $P_{T_e}$ is the electron-temperature peaking ratio, $T_e$ is the
local electron temperature, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the position of
the magnetic axis, $\langle T_e\rangle_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}$ is the
volume-averaged electron temperature, $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the
plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, $\mathbf{x}$ is a
position within that volume, and $\mathrm{d}^3\mathbf{x}$ is the
differential volume element.

The numerator is the temperature evaluated specifically at the magnetic
axis, represented by [electron temperature at magnetic
axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis). The denominator is a
volume average over the confined plasma volume up to the last closed flux
surface; it is not a local value, a point maximum, or an average over other
plasma populations. The ratio applies only to the electron population and
does not represent ion-temperature peaking.

This quantity is obtained by dividing the magnetic-axis electron temperature
by the corresponding volume-averaged electron temperature, so it is distinct
from either operand alone and quantifies the relative central peaking of the
electron-temperature distribution.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short:
Major-radius coordinate assigned to the selected flux surface, defined as
the midpoint between its minimum and maximum cylindrical R values.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the representative major-radius location of the selected
flux surface, rather than the radial coordinate of one particular point. It
summarizes the surface’s inboard and outboard radial extent in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

It is defined as the midpoint of the minimum and maximum major-radius
coordinates on the selected flux surface:

$$
R_{\rm fs} = \frac{R_{\min} + R_{\max}}{2}
$$

where $R_{\rm fs}$ is the representative radial coordinate of the flux
surface, and $R_{\min}$ and $R_{\max}$ are respectively the minimum and
maximum values of the cylindrical major-radius coordinate over that surface.

The definition applies to the complete selected flux surface and uses the
extrema midpoint as its aggregation convention; it is not an area-weighted,
volume-weighted, or flux-weighted average. It does not denote the radial
coordinate of a particular point, such as the magnetic axis or a specified
midplane location.

This quantity is the flux-surface specialization of the parent [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate). It differs from the [normalized minor
radius of a flux surface](name:normalized_minor_radius_of_flux_surface),
which characterizes minor-radius position relative to a reference length
rather than the surface’s major-radius location.

NAMES.name: reference_magnetic_field
NAMES.short:
Reference magnetic-field vector of the equilibrium magnetic induction
evaluated at the reference point, retaining field strength and direction
before selecting a component such as the toroidal reference magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The reference magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_{\rm ref}$ is the equilibrium
[magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) evaluated at the reference point
used to define a local field reference. It represents the vector field at
that locus, retaining both field strength and direction rather than
selecting a cylindrical component or scalar magnitude.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the reference field may
be resolved as

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\rm ref}=B_{R,{\rm ref}}\hat{R}+B_{\phi,{\rm ref}}\hat{\phi}+B_{Z,{\rm ref}}\hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}_{\rm ref}$ is the reference magnetic field, $B_{R,{\rm
ref}}$ is its signed radial component, $B_{\phi,{\rm ref}}$ is the [toroidal
reference magnetic field](name:toroidal_reference_magnetic_field),
$B_{Z,{\rm ref}}$ is its signed vertical component, and $\hat{R}$,
$\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ are the basis vectors for increasing major
radius, toroidal angle, and vertical height.

This quantity is defined at the reference point for the equilibrium field;
it is not the spatially unrestricted local [magnetic
induction](name:magnetic_field). It has no species population, and its
aggregation convention is a point value at the reference locus, not a
spatial average or finite-volume reduction.

The parent quantity is distinct from component-resolved reference fields:
the [toroidal reference magnetic
field](name:toroidal_reference_magnetic_field) is its projection along
$\hat{\phi}$ at the reference point, not a separate vector field. It is also
distinct from the unrestricted [toroidal magnetic
field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), which does not by name impose the
reference locus.
NAMES.sign:
Positive when a resolved component of $\mathbf{B}_{\rm
ref}$ points along the corresponding positive basis vector of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where the positive directions
are increasing major radius $R$, increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and
increasing vertical height $Z$.
